title: 561. The Golden Age of Japan: Secrets of the Imperial Court (Part 2)

sentences.en: In spring, the dawn, when the slowly paling mountain rim is tinged with red and wisps of faintly crimson-purple cloud float in the sky.
sentences.zh: 春天是破晓的时候。渐渐发白的山峦，透出微红的色彩，紫红色的云彩在天空中飘荡，这真是美极了。

sentences.en: In summer, the night.
sentences.zh: 夏天是夜晚。

sentences.en: Moonlit nights, of course, but also at the dark of the moon.
sentences.zh: 月色皎洁的夜晚固然好，即便是在没有月亮的漆黑之夜，也别有一番风味。

sentences.en: It's beautiful when fireflies are dancing everywhere in a mazy flight.
sentences.zh: 萤火虫到处乱飞，那景象真是美妙。

sentences.en: And it's delightful to see just one or two fly through the darkness, glowing softly.
sentences.zh: 若是只有一两只萤火虫在黑暗中发出微弱的光芒，缓缓飞过，也令人感到愉悦。

sentences.en: Rain falling on a summer night is also lovely.
sentences.zh: 夏夜的雨也是可爱的。

sentences.en: In autumn, the evening, the blazing sun has sunk very close to the mountain rim.
sentences.zh: 秋天是黄昏。夕阳照耀，红彤彤的太阳，近在山峦边缘。

sentences.en: And now even the crows in threes and fours or twos and threes, hurrying to their roost, are a moving sight.
sentences.zh: 这时，连乌鸦三三两两地赶回巢去，也显得十分动人。

sentences.en: Still more enchanting is the sight of a string of wild geese in the distant sky, very tiny.
sentences.zh: 更令人着迷的是，远方的天空中，一行大雁排成小小的队列，看起来非常可爱。

sentences.en: And oh, how inexpressible, when the sun has sunk, to hear in the growing darkness the wind and the song of autumn insects.
sentences.zh: 啊，太阳落山后，在渐浓的夜色中，听着风声和秋虫的鸣叫，那种意境真是难以言表。

sentences.en: In winter, the early morning, if snow is falling, of course, it's unutterably delightful.
sentences.zh: 冬天是清晨。若是下着雪，那自然是美得无法形容。

sentences.en: But it's perfect, too, if there's a pure white frost, or even just when it's very cold, and they hasten to build up the fires in the braziers and carry in fresh charcoal.
sentences.zh: 若是结了白霜，或者仅仅是天气寒冷，人们匆忙地生起火盆，搬来新鲜的木炭，那也是极好的。

sentences.en: But it's unpleasant, as the day draws on and the air grows warmer, how the brazier fire dies down to white ash.
sentences.zh: 但到了白天，天气转暖，火盆里的火渐渐熄灭，只剩下白色的灰烬，这就不太讨人喜欢了。

sentences.en: So that, ladies and gentlemen, is one of the most famous passages in all Japanese literature.
sentences.zh: 所以，女士们、先生们，这就是日本文学史上最著名的篇章之一。

sentences.en: I would argue one of the most extraordinary passages of prose you will ever read.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是你所读过的最非凡的散文篇章之一。

sentences.en: It is the beginning of a really, really remarkable and original masterpiece called The Pillow Book, which was written in the early years of the 11th century in what is now Kyoto.
sentences.zh: 这是那部真正令人惊叹且独具匠心的杰作《枕草子》的开篇，它写于11世纪初，地点就在今天的京都。

sentences.en: And, Tom, we talked last time about the great Japanese classic, The Tale of Genji.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，上次我们谈到了日本的伟大经典《源氏物语》。

sentences.en: This was written round about the same time in what was then called Heian Kyo.
sentences.zh: 那部作品大约也是在同一时期，在当时被称为平安京的地方写成的。

sentences.en: And as with The Tale of Genji, its author was a woman.
sentences.zh: 和《源氏物语》一样，它的作者也是一位女性。

sentences.en: Yes, the woman was called Seishonagon.
sentences.zh: 是的，这位女性名叫清少纳言。

sentences.en: And Murasaki Shikabu, the author of The Tale of Genji, knew Seishonagon and didn't like her.
sentences.zh: 而《源氏物语》的作者紫式部认识清少纳言，而且不喜欢她。

sentences.en: So she wrote in her diary, Seishonagon was dreadfully conceited.
sentences.zh: 所以她在日记里写道，清少纳言真是自负得可怕。

sentences.en: She thought herself so clever and littered her writings with Chinese characters.
sentences.zh: 她自以为很聪明，在文章里堆砌汉字。

sentences.en: But if you examine them closely, they left a great deal to be desired.
sentences.zh: 但如果你仔细审视，会发现她的文章还有很多不足之处。

sentences.en: So like a kind of negative review of our podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这就像是对我们播客的一种负面评价。

sentences.en: Left by the hosts of an inferior Goalhanger podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 由某个劣质Goalhanger播客的主持人留下的评价。

sentences.en: No doubt.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: Although, of course, I mean, you know, Murasaki and Seishonagon are both transcendent geniuses.
sentences.zh: 虽然，当然，我的意思是，你知道，紫式部和清少纳言都是超越时代的天才。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So actually, the analogy doesn't work at all.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，这个类比根本不成立。

sentences.en: It breaks down there.
sentences.zh: 在这里就说不通了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So I think what you get there is a clear tone of envy.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为你从中读出了一种明显的嫉妒语气。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, we're concerns of tones of envy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，我们很在意这种嫉妒的语气。

sentences.en: We are.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I guess it's not surprising, actually, because the two women are in lots of ways quite alike.
sentences.zh: 我想这其实并不奇怪，因为这两位女性在很多方面都很相似。

sentences.en: So Seishonagon, Se is a family name, but Seishonagon, like Shikabu, so Murasaki's kind of second name, is the name of a post in the Imperial Civil Service.
sentences.zh: 清少纳言，“清”是姓氏，而“少纳言”和“式部”一样，是紫式部的名字，其实是朝廷文官职位名称。

sentences.en: So like Murasaki Shikabu, Seishonagon is the daughter of a functionary, of a civil servant.
sentences.zh: 所以就像紫式部一样，清少纳言也是一位官员的女儿。

sentences.en: And Murasaki knew about Seishonagon because they had both served as kind of ladies-in-waiting to an empress in the Imperial Court.
sentences.zh: 紫式部了解清少纳言，是因为她们都曾在皇宫里担任过皇后的女官。

sentences.en: And also, like Murasaki, Seishonagon knew Chinese.
sentences.zh: 而且，和紫式部一样，清少纳言也懂汉文。

sentences.en: We talked about this in the previous episode, that for a woman to know Chinese, seen as very unladylike, very unbecoming.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一集谈过，当时女性懂汉文被认为是非常不淑女、非常不得体的。

sentences.en: And Murasaki tried to keep her knowledge of Chinese secret.
sentences.zh: 紫式部试图隐藏她懂汉文的事实。

sentences.en: You know, she was embarrassed by it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她为此感到尴尬。

sentences.en: Her fellow ladies-in-waiting teased her about it.
sentences.zh: 她的女官同僚们还因此取笑她。

sentences.en: But Seishonagon did not veil it.
sentences.zh: 但清少纳言并没有掩饰。

sentences.en: She absolutely paraded her knowledge of Chinese.
sentences.zh: 她完全是在炫耀自己对汉文的精通。

sentences.en: She's absolutely unafraid to make a show of her brilliance.
sentences.zh: 她丝毫不畏惧展示自己的才华。

sentences.en: And she does it with such style and charisma that it clearly makes her a kind of a massive star at court.
sentences.zh: 而且她以一种如此有风格和魅力的方式去做，显然使她成为了宫廷里的一颗耀眼明星。

sentences.en: So, unlike Murasaki, she boasts of how ready she is to kind of stand up and be the centre of attention.
sentences.zh: 所以，与紫式部不同，她夸耀自己是多么乐于站出来成为关注的焦点。

sentences.en: So she writes in the Pillow Book, I am not renowned for my modesty or prudence.
sentences.zh: 她在《枕草子》中写道：我并不以谦虚或谨慎而闻名。

sentences.en: So, again, the comparison between Seishonagon, who's not renowned for her modesty, and the presenters of the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 所以，再次回到清少纳言（她并不以谦虚闻名）与我们这些主持人的比较上。

sentences.en: That rather breaks down there, doesn't it, Tom?
sentences.zh: 那里的比较确实站不住脚，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: We're very shy and retiring like Murasaki.
sentences.zh: 我们像紫式部一样害羞且内向。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Now, we talked last time when we were explaining about the tale of Genji and this world of kind of 9th, 10th, 11th century Japan.
sentences.zh: 上次我们解释《源氏物语》和9、10、11世纪日本那个世界时谈到了这一点。

sentences.en: We sort of talked about what a remarkable book it is to read.
sentences.zh: 我们谈到了这是一本多么了不起的书。

sentences.en: And I have to say, in many ways, I think the Pillow Book is even more remarkable.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，在很多方面，我认为《枕草子》甚至更了不起。

sentences.en: So I've been reading it over the last few days.
sentences.zh: 过去几天我一直在读它。

sentences.en: And what shines through on every page is the wit, the brilliance, the sophistication, the charm,
sentences.zh: 每一页都闪耀着智慧、才华、世故、魅力，

sentences.en: and the individual personality of the author in a way that I don't think I've ever encountered with any other work of medieval literature.
sentences.zh: 以及作者独特的个性，这种感觉我在任何其他中世纪文学作品中都未曾遇到过。

sentences.en: I mean, this really is Seishonagon's book.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这真的是清少纳言的书。

sentences.en: And you feel that you know her when you're reading it in a way you don't with any other author at the time.
sentences.zh: 当你阅读它时，你会觉得你认识她，这种感觉在阅读同时代其他作者的作品时是不会有的。

sentences.en: I mean, I can't think of any work of ancient or medieval literature where charm and wit, as you say, is manifest on every page.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想不出还有哪部古代或中世纪文学作品，像你所说的那样，魅力和智慧在每一页都显而易见。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not what you associate, really, with kind of ancient literature.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这并不是你通常与古代文学联系在一起的东西。

sentences.en: And as you say, her personality is so vivid that you feel like you completely know her.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，她的个性如此鲜活，让你觉得完全了解她。

sentences.en: And I agree that, like the tale of Genji, it feels dislocating.
sentences.zh: 我同意，就像《源氏物语》一样，它让人有一种时空错乱感。

sentences.en: You have to keep pinching yourself and reminding yourself this is someone who's writing.
sentences.zh: 你必须不断掐自己，提醒自己这是一个正在写作的人。

sentences.en: You know, keep saying this.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一直在说这个。

sentences.en: In England, this is the Anglo-Saxon period.
sentences.zh: 在英国，这还是盎格鲁-撒克逊时期。

sentences.en: I mean, it is amazing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太神奇了。

sentences.en: So how did she come to write it?
sentences.zh: 那么她是怎样写出这本书的呢？

sentences.en: Because that in itself is a remarkable story.
sentences.zh: 因为这本身就是一个非凡的故事。

sentences.en: Yes, and may well be made up.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且很可能是编造的。

sentences.en: So this is part of the fun of reading the Pillow Book is that Seishonagon is very, she's very playful.
sentences.zh: 这就是阅读《枕草子》的乐趣所在，清少纳言非常、非常调皮。

sentences.en: You can never entirely trust what she's saying, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为你永远不能完全相信她所说的话。

sentences.en: So the name Pillow Book, it comes from the story of how she comes to write it.
sentences.zh: “枕草子”这个名字，来源于她写这本书的故事。

sentences.en: So the story she gives is that a minister comes to the empress who is Seishonagon's mistress, presents the empress with a great sheaf of paper.
sentences.zh: 她讲述的故事是，一位大臣来到清少纳言侍奉的皇后那里，送给皇后一大叠纸。

sentences.en: And the empress makes a gift of it to, say, Shonagon.
sentences.zh: 皇后把这些纸赏赐给了少纳言。

sentences.en: And she uses this paper to start recording observations, thoughts, experiences, whatever.
sentences.zh: 于是她用这些纸开始记录观察、想法、经历，等等。

sentences.en: And she seems to have kept the sheaf of papers either under or next to her pillow.
sentences.zh: 她似乎把这叠纸放在枕头下或枕头旁边。

sentences.en: And she then leaves the court and continues to write it.
sentences.zh: 后来她离开了宫廷，继续写作。

sentences.en: And then one day, oh me, oh my, she is disturbed by a governor who comes to pay his respects to her.
sentences.zh: 有一天，哎呀，天哪，一位前来拜访的国司打扰了她。

sentences.en: And so she pulls out the pillow for the governor to sit on.
sentences.zh: 于是她把枕头抽出来给国司坐。

sentences.en: And there are the sheaf of papers.
sentences.zh: 那叠纸就在那里。

sentences.en: And Seishonagon is so mortified.
sentences.zh: 清少纳言感到非常羞愧。

sentences.en: I scrambled to try and retrieve them, but he carried them off with him and kept them for a very long time before returning them.
sentences.zh: 我手忙脚乱地想把它们拿回来，但他把它们带走了，并保存了很长一段时间才还给我。

sentences.en: That seems to have been the moment when this book first become known.
sentences.zh: 那似乎就是这本书第一次为人所知的时候。

sentences.en: And she says, I'm mortified, mortified that it's got out.
sentences.zh: 她说，我感到羞愧，羞愧于它被传了出去。

sentences.en: It's terrible that people have read this masterpiece that I've written.
sentences.zh: 我写出的这部杰作被人们读到了，真是太糟糕了。

sentences.en: And clearly, she's making play with the expectation that she, as a woman, was supposed to be mortified.
sentences.zh: 显然，她是在利用人们对她作为女性应该感到羞愧的预期来开玩笑。

sentences.en: And this is kind of typical of the, I guess, the kind of the subtlety and the ambivalence that characterizes her humor throughout the book.
sentences.zh: 这大概是她贯穿全书的幽默感中那种微妙和矛盾的典型表现。

sentences.en: So let's, for people who've not read it, which I'm guessing is most people listen to the show, let's explain exactly what it is.
sentences.zh: 那么，对于那些没读过的人——我猜大多数听这个节目的人都没读过——让我们解释一下它到底是什么。

sentences.en: Because, as you said, it's bonkers to think that while she is writing this, Ethered the Unready is paying Dane Gale to Olaf Trigvason.
sentences.zh: 因为正如你所说，想到她在写这本书的同时，埃塞尔雷德二世正在向奥拉夫·特里格瓦松支付丹麦金，这简直太疯狂了。

sentences.en: And to give people a sense, it's a kind of a compilation of diary entries, journal entries, random thoughts about nature and the seasons, anecdotes about the imperial court,
sentences.zh: 为了让大家有个概念，它是一部日记条目、随笔、关于自然和季节的随机想法、关于皇宫的轶事、

sentences.en: stories of love and romance, all jumbled together.
sentences.zh: 爱情和浪漫故事的汇编，所有这些都混杂在一起。

sentences.en: So you never know what's going to be next in each entry.
sentences.zh: 所以你永远不知道每一条接下来会写什么。

sentences.en: I mean, The Tale of Genji, you can recognize it as a novel, but The Pillow Book is unlike really anything that's been written since.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，《源氏物语》你可以把它看作是一部小说，但《枕草子》与此后写出的任何作品都不同。

sentences.en: And I guess if you had to compare it to anything, perhaps to a blog, perhaps even to a kind of, you know, the best kind of podcast you could possibly imagine,
sentences.zh: 我想如果你非要把它和什么东西比较，也许是博客，甚至可能是某种，你知道，你能想象到的最好的播客，

sentences.en: where it's constantly kind of going off on various tangents.
sentences.zh: 它总是会偏离到各种各样的话题上。

sentences.en: But every tangent is completely fascinating.
sentences.zh: 但每一个话题都完全令人着迷。

sentences.en: So the genius of it for, say, Shonagun is that essentially it's a framework in which she can write about anything that interests her.
sentences.zh: 所以对清少纳言来说，它的天才之处在于，它本质上是一个框架，让她可以写任何她感兴趣的东西。

sentences.en: So you get lyrical descriptions of the kind with which you open.
sentences.zh: 所以你会看到她开篇那种抒情的描写。

sentences.en: And often these are descriptions of things that make her happy.
sentences.zh: 而且这些往往是让她感到快乐的事物的描写。

sentences.en: And the sense of happiness that she conveys is something that I think people could still identify with today.
sentences.zh: 她所传达的那种幸福感，我认为人们今天仍然能产生共鸣。

sentences.en: So how delightful it is in winter on a fiercely cold night when you're lying there listening, snuggled far down under the bedclothes,
sentences.zh: 比如，冬天在寒冷的夜晚，躺在被窝里，蜷缩在被褥深处，听着声音是多么令人愉悦，

sentences.en: and the sound of a temple bell comes to you with such a deep and distant reverberation that it seems to be emerging from somewhere buried.
sentences.zh: 寺庙的钟声传来，带着如此深沉而遥远的余音，仿佛是从地底深处发出来的。

sentences.en: So you're simultaneously there in 11th century Japan, the sense of a bell ringing.
sentences.zh: 所以你同时身处11世纪的日本，感受着钟声的鸣响。

sentences.en: But also, I mean, that is a universal experience, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但同时，我的意思是，那是一种普遍的体验，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, the joy of being warm in bed in a cold night.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在寒冷的夜晚睡在温暖的被窝里的快乐。

sentences.en: I mean, it's incredible.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: The other thing, she loves a liSt.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，她喜欢列清单。

sentences.en: And actually, when I was in Japan, I realized that this is a continuing thing in Japan.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当我在日本时，我意识到这在日本是一种持续存在的现象。

sentences.en: So you go to a castle and say, this is the fourth best castle in Japan or that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 你去一座城堡，他们会说，这是日本第四好的城堡，诸如此类。

sentences.en: You know, they love it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们很喜欢这样。

sentences.en: And it clearly begins with, say, Shonagon.
sentences.zh: 这显然是从清少纳言开始的。

sentences.en: So she will list, you know, top mountains, top ponds, top horses, all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 所以她会列出，你知道，最好的山、最好的池塘、最好的马，所有这类东西。

sentences.en: Her list of top birds.
sentences.zh: 她列出的最好的鸟。

sentences.en: She's not keen on the heron.
sentences.zh: 她不太喜欢苍鹭。

sentences.en: She says the heron looks horrible.
sentences.zh: 她说苍鹭看起来很可怕。

sentences.en: Horrible, yeah.
sentences.zh: 很可怕，是的。

sentences.en: Very keen on the mandarin duck, which she says is very touching in the way the pair will change places on cold nights to brush the frost from each other's wings.
sentences.zh: 她非常喜欢鸳鸯，她说鸳鸯在寒冷的夜晚互相换位置，拂去对方翅膀上的霜，这种方式非常感人。

sentences.en: And I think the Japanese generally are very keen on the mandarin duck because it seems to have been an emblem of marital fidelity.
sentences.zh: 我认为日本人通常非常喜欢鸳鸯，因为它似乎一直是夫妻忠贞的象征。

sentences.en: So Genji, in Murasaki's novel, he's walking out under the moonlight with Murasaki, his great love, and he hears a mandarin duck.
sentences.zh: 所以紫式部小说里的源氏，在月光下与他挚爱的紫之上散步时，听到了鸳鸯的声音。

sentences.en: He has this great Proustian rush of memory, thinking of all the times that he's spent with Murasaki.
sentences.zh: 他产生了一种普鲁斯特式的记忆冲击，想起了他与紫之上共度的所有时光。

sentences.en: And it brings back fond memories of times now gone by.
sentences.zh: 这勾起了他对逝去时光的美好回忆。

sentences.en: But the best things are the lists that are simultaneously bonkers, but also the kind of things that people write on social media or on blogs.
sentences.zh: 但最棒的是那些既疯狂，又像人们在社交媒体或博客上写的东西一样的清单。

sentences.en: Kind of listicles.
sentences.zh: 类似于清单体文章。

sentences.en: Yeah, listicles.
sentences.zh: 是的，清单体文章。

sentences.en: So you've got some of your favourites written down.
sentences.zh: 所以你记下了一些你最喜欢的。

sentences.en: So a couple of mine are, she's got a list of things people despise, one of which is people who have a reputation for being exceptionally good-natured.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的几个是，她列出了一些人们鄙视的事物，其中之一是那些以性格特别好而闻名的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's kind of almost like Oscar Wilde, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这简直就像奥斯卡·王尔德，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Or rare things.
sentences.zh: 或者稀有的事物。

sentences.en: A son-in-law who is praised by his wife's father.
sentences.zh: 被岳父称赞的女婿。

sentences.en: Likewise, a wife who is loved by her mother-in-law.
sentences.zh: 同样，被婆婆疼爱的儿媳。

sentences.en: And then the next entry under rare things she's written is, a pair of silver tweezers that can actually pull out hairs properly.
sentences.zh: 然后她在“稀有的事物”条目下写的下一条是，一把能真正把毛发拔干净的银镊子。

sentences.en: And embarrassing things.
sentences.zh: 还有令人尴尬的事物。

sentences.en: And this will be so familiar, I think, to anyone who has ever been at the school gates.
sentences.zh: 我想，任何去过学校门口的人都会对此感到非常熟悉。

sentences.en: Someone insists on telling you about some horrid little child carried away with her own infatuation with the creature,
sentences.zh: 有人坚持要告诉你关于某个讨厌的小孩的事，她沉浸在自己对这个生物的迷恋中，

sentences.en: imitating its voice as she gushes about the cute and winning things it says.
sentences.zh: 模仿着它的声音，滔滔不绝地讲述它说的那些可爱又动人的话。

sentences.en: And Seishoenigan generally doesn't seem to have been very fond of children.
sentences.zh: 清少纳言似乎通常不太喜欢孩子。

sentences.en: So she also accuses three-year-olds of being smug and cocky.
sentences.zh: 所以她还指责三岁的孩子自以为是、傲慢自大。

sentences.en: Which is, I mean, she's not wrong.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她说得没错。

sentences.en: And so you've got all these incredible lists.
sentences.zh: 所以你拥有所有这些不可思议的清单。

sentences.en: Repulsive things.
sentences.zh: 令人反感的事物。

sentences.en: You see that?
sentences.zh: 你看到了吗？

sentences.en: Repulsive things.
sentences.zh: 令人反感的事物。

sentences.en: The inside of a cat's ear.
sentences.zh: 猫耳朵的里面。

sentences.en: I mean, that's true.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是真的。

sentences.en: But also, I love this one.
sentences.zh: 但我也很喜欢这一段。

sentences.en: The way a man must feel when his wife, who he's not really very fond of, is ill for a long time.
sentences.zh: 当一个男人对自己的妻子并没有多少感情，而她又久病缠身时，他心里会是什么滋味呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's wonderful.
sentences.zh: 没错，这太奇妙了。

sentences.en: And also, there are kind of brilliant anecdotes about court life.
sentences.zh: 而且，书中还有一些关于宫廷生活的精彩轶事。

sentences.en: So there's an amazing story, for instance, about how there's a great snowfall.
sentences.zh: 比如，有一个非常棒的故事，讲的是当时下了一场大雪。

sentences.en: And the gardeners sweep up all the snow and they make a huge snow mountain.
sentences.zh: 园丁们把雪扫到一起，堆成了一座巨大的雪山。

sentences.en: And the empress and all her ladies-in-waiting, including Seishoenigan, have a kind of sweepstake on how long this snow mountain will last before it melts.
sentences.zh: 皇后和所有的女官，包括清少纳言在内，打赌这座雪山能维持多久才融化。

sentences.en: And Seishoenigan says, oh, it'll last for weeks, weeks and weeks.
sentences.zh: 清少纳言说，哦，它能维持好几周，好几周呢。

sentences.en: And everyone says, no, that's mad.
sentences.zh: 大家都说，不，那太疯狂了。

sentences.en: You'll never do that.
sentences.zh: 你绝对做不到的。

sentences.en: And she has a bet with the empress.
sentences.zh: 于是她和皇后打了个赌。

sentences.en: And Seishoenigan described, you know, every day she goes to inspect the state of the snow mountain.
sentences.zh: 清少纳言描述说，她每天都会去查看雪山的状态。

sentences.en: And gradually, over the course of the weeks, it gets dirtier and dirtier and dirtier until it's completely black.
sentences.zh: 几周过去了，雪山变得越来越脏，最后完全变成了黑色。

sentences.en: But it's still very solid there.
sentences.zh: 但它依然非常坚固。

sentences.en: And she has a gardener who comes to report, you know, on the state of the mountain and everything.
sentences.zh: 她还让园丁来向她汇报雪山的情况等等。

sentences.en: And the evening before, it's still there.
sentences.zh: 前一天晚上，雪山还在那儿。

sentences.en: She's clearly going to win the bet.
sentences.zh: 她显然要赢下这场赌局了。

sentences.en: And in the morning, the gardener says, it's gone.
sentences.zh: 可到了早上，园丁却说，雪山不见了。

sentences.en: It's been vanished.
sentences.zh: 它消失了。

sentences.en: And it turns out that the empress has had people come in and sweep it away and cheat and Seishoenigan goes and complains to the emperor about this.
sentences.zh: 原来是皇后派人把它扫走了，耍了赖，清少纳言就去向天皇告状。

sentences.en: And he smiles and remarks, well, I suppose she just didn't want to see you win.
sentences.zh: 天皇笑了笑说，嗯，我想她只是不想看你赢吧。

sentences.en: And to think that this is an 11th century court, I mean, that kind of anecdote, you know, we said this in the last episode.
sentences.zh: 想到这可是11世纪的宫廷，我的意思是，这种轶事，就像我们在上一集里说的那样。

sentences.en: What wouldn't you give for a story like that from the court of Edward the Confessor or something?
sentences.zh: 如果能从忏悔者爱德华的宫廷里听到这样的故事，你愿意付出什么代价呢？

sentences.en: But in a way,
sentences.zh: 但在某种程度上，

sentences.en: you couldn't have had a story like that because a literary document like that to come from the court of Edward the Confessor or any kind of early medieval European court would just seem unthinkable,
sentences.zh: 你不可能有这样的故事，因为像这样出自忏悔者爱德华宫廷或任何早期中世纪欧洲宫廷的文学文献，简直是不可想象的，

sentences.en: wouldn't it?
sentences.zh: 不是吗？

sentences.en: It would seem impossible.
sentences.zh: 这看起来是不可能的。

sentences.en: But as we said last time, it comes from a very specific set of circumstances.
sentences.zh: 但正如我们上次所说，它源于一套非常特殊的背景。

sentences.en: And I guess the misleading thing when we read this is we think of Seishoenigan as our contemporary,
sentences.zh: 我想，我们在阅读时容易产生误解，是因为我们把清少纳言当成了我们同时代的人，

sentences.en: because we can recognize so much of what she's saying about the relations between parents and children and about annoying things that people do and tweezers that don't work properly and all of these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 因为她所说的关于亲子关系、人们做的烦人琐事、不好用的镊子等等，我们都能感同身受。

sentences.en: But she is still very alien.
sentences.zh: 但她依然非常陌生。

sentences.en: I mean, she's from a world that could not seem more alien.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她来自一个看起来再陌生不过的世界。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And she is clearly a product of the court culture that she adorns.
sentences.zh: 她显然是她所点缀的那种宫廷文化的产物。

sentences.en: And I think it's evident that she is giving court culture the best spin that she possibly can.
sentences.zh: 我认为显而易见的是，她正在尽其所能地美化这种宫廷文化。

sentences.en: And I think that's probably because she does love it, because she is such a brilliant figure at court.
sentences.zh: 我想这大概是因为她确实热爱它，因为她是宫廷里一位如此出色的风云人物。

sentences.en: I mean, that's, you know, that's wonderful.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那，你知道，那太棒了。

sentences.en: And so there's this word, apparently, again, marshalling my fluent Japanese, akashi, which can be translated as delightful, amusing, charming, fun, I suppose, exquisite, whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以有一个词，显然，再次发挥我流利的日语水平，叫“可怜”（akashi），可以翻译为令人愉悦、有趣、迷人、好玩，我想，精致，随你怎么说。

sentences.en: And this is essentially the word she uses to describe so many things that happen at court.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是她用来描述宫廷里发生的许多事情的词。

sentences.en: But when you look at Murasaki's diary, which is a kind of parallel to the Pillow book, she's much more introverted, much more morose, I think.
sentences.zh: 但当你看看紫式部的日记，那算是《枕草子》的平行篇，我觉得她要内向得多，也忧郁得多。

sentences.en: And she gives a darker portrait of life at court.
sentences.zh: 她对宫廷生活的描绘更加阴暗。

sentences.en: So Seishoenigan adores gossip.
sentences.zh: 清少纳言热爱八卦。

sentences.en: I mean, she praises it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她对此大加赞赏。

sentences.en: What could possibly be more fun than talking about other people and criticising them, she writes.
sentences.zh: 她写道，还有什么比谈论别人并批评他们更有趣的呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, she's not wrong.
sentences.zh: 没错，她说得没错。

sentences.en: Whereas Murasaki beats herself up about being a gossip.
sentences.zh: 而紫式部则因为自己爱八卦而自责。

sentences.en: And unlike her rival, she, you know, she confesses to loneliness, to isolation.
sentences.zh: 而且与她的对手不同，她承认自己感到孤独和孤立。

sentences.en: There's no doubt which of those women would fit in well as a guest on the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，这两位女性中，哪一位更适合作为嘉宾参加《历史的其余部分》节目。

sentences.en: Well, yeah, you're probably right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，你大概是对的。

sentences.en: But I think when you combine, say, the writings of these two extraordinary authors, what you get is a sense that this court is kind of, if you want to say,
sentences.zh: 但我认为，当你把这两位非凡作家的作品结合起来看时，你会感觉到这个宫廷，如果你想说的话，

sentences.en: civilised to the nth degree.
sentences.zh: 文明程度极高。

sentences.en: I mean, it's kind of the epitome of civilisation.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直是文明的缩影。

sentences.en: And when the Japanese, as they have done ever since the 11th century, celebrate the Heian court as the kind of the great classical age of elegance, of sophistication, of style.
sentences.zh: 当日本人自11世纪以来一直赞美平安时代为优雅、精致、风尚的伟大古典时代时，

sentences.en: I mean, they're not wrong.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们并没有错。

sentences.en: And, Dominic, we, after this episode, we're going to be embarking on a six-part series on the life of Peter the Great.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，在这一集之后，我们将开始制作关于彼得大帝生平的六集系列节目。

sentences.en: And there is a lot of kind of malarkey with drunk bears and bellows being shoved up bottoms and things.
sentences.zh: 那里有很多乱七八糟的事情，比如醉酒的熊，还有把风箱塞进屁股里的事儿。

sentences.en: Peter the Great's court is not elegant.
sentences.zh: 彼得大帝的宫廷可不优雅。

sentences.en: This court absolutely is.
sentences.zh: 而这个宫廷绝对是优雅的。

sentences.en: That really would be a culture clash if these women are pitched up at the court of Peter the Great.
sentences.zh: 如果让这些女性出现在彼得大帝的宫廷里，那真会是一场文化冲突。

sentences.en: I suspect Sei Shonigan would have done quite well, but Murasaki probably would have hated it.
sentences.zh: 我怀疑清少纳言会过得不错，但紫式部可能会讨厌那里。

sentences.en: So, Tom, a very good example of that degree of sophistication and kind of elegance is poetry.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，这种精致和优雅程度的一个很好的例子就是诗歌。

sentences.en: And poetry matters enormously to Sei Shonigan, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 诗歌对清少纳言来说非常重要，不是吗？

sentences.en: As it does to Genji in The Tale of Genji.
sentences.zh: 就像它对《源氏物语》中的源氏一样重要。

sentences.en: Yeah, so Genji is a brilliant poet.
sentences.zh: 是的，源氏是一位出色的诗人。

sentences.en: And it has a significance that we might, in the 21st century, in Britain, or indeed in any Western country, really struggle to understand.
sentences.zh: 这种重要性，我们在21世纪的英国，或者任何西方国家，可能真的很难理解。

sentences.en: Because mastery of poetry is enormously important as a badge of status and as a badge of elegance.
sentences.zh: 因为精通诗歌作为一种地位和优雅的象征，极其重要。

sentences.en: I mean, to be a desirable, attractive person, an impressive person, you should be able to quote poems and come up with poems on the spot.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，要成为一个令人向往、有吸引力、令人印象深刻的人，你应该能够引用诗句，并能即兴创作诗歌。

sentences.en: But also of your ability.
sentences.zh: 而且还要看你的能力。

sentences.en: I mean, it's kind of, you know, people today have to have a mastery of IT or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这有点像，你知道，今天的人们必须精通IT技术之类的。

sentences.en: In the Hayan court, you have to have a mastery of poetry.
sentences.zh: 在平安时代的宫廷里，你必须精通诗歌。

sentences.en: And to quote Ivan Morris,
sentences.zh: 引用伊万·莫里斯的话，

sentences.en: And so this is a crucial part of Sei Shonigan's fame at the court, is she's not just a brilliant poet, but she's also very, very knowledgeable about poetry.
sentences.zh: 这是清少纳言在宫廷中声名鹊起的关键，她不仅是一位出色的诗人，而且对诗歌也非常非常了解。

sentences.en: And so if someone sends in a quote, she can rework it, she can refashion it in a kind of exquisitely witty way.
sentences.zh: 所以如果有人发来一句诗，她可以对其进行重写，以一种极其机智的方式重新塑造它。

sentences.en: And it's no wonder that Murasaki hates her, because she's just brilliant at it.
sentences.zh: 难怪紫式部讨厌她，因为她在这方面简直太天才了。

sentences.en: It imposes incredible strain, because if you mess it up, you know, if you misquote something, if your poem is felt not quite to hit the mark,
sentences.zh: 这带来了难以置信的压力，因为如果你搞砸了，你知道，如果你引用错误，如果你的诗被认为不够出彩，

sentences.en: then that's terribly damaging to your reputation.
sentences.zh: 那对你的名声将是极大的损害。

sentences.en: And even say, Shonigan admits this.
sentences.zh: 甚至连清少纳言也承认这一点。

sentences.en: So somebody sends a poem, you become very anxious when you have to make a quick response to someone's poem.
sentences.zh: 所以有人寄来一首诗，当你必须对别人的诗做出快速回应时，你会变得非常焦虑。

sentences.en: And you can't come up with anything.
sentences.zh: 而你却什么也想不出来。

sentences.en: If it's a lover, there's no particular need to hurry to send a reply.
sentences.zh: 如果是情人，没必要急着回复。

sentences.en: But there are times when circumstances make it necessary.
sentences.zh: 但有时环境使然，不得不回。

sentences.en: And if it's some exchange with a lady, nothing special, and you feel you can just dash something off, that's precisely when you're inclined to make an unfortunate blunder.
sentences.zh: 如果这只是和某位女士的交流，没什么特别的，你觉得可以随便写点什么应付过去，那恰恰是你容易犯下不幸错误的时候。

sentences.en: So it gives a really vivid sense of, you know, the tension of not losing status and rank by sending out a kind of dud few lines.
sentences.zh: 所以这让人非常真切地感受到，那种因为写出几行烂诗而失去地位和等级的紧张感。

sentences.en: Well, there's an amazing scene very early in the book, where the empress says to, she folds up a piece of paper, and she says to all her kind of ladies-in-waiting, her courtiers,
sentences.zh: 嗯，书的开头有一个很棒的场景，皇后折起一张纸，对她所有的女官、朝臣说，

sentences.en: Now, I want each of you to write here the first ancient poem that springs to mind.
sentences.zh: 现在，我要你们每个人在这里写下脑海中浮现的第一首古诗。

sentences.en: And Shonigan is in a complete and utter panic, and she says to a male official, What on earth can I write?
sentences.zh: 清少纳言陷入了彻底的恐慌，她对一位男性官员说，我到底能写什么？

sentences.en: And he pushes her the paper back.
sentences.zh: 他把纸推回给她。

sentences.en: He says, Quick, write something down yourself for Her Majesty.
sentences.zh: 他说，快，你自己为皇后写点什么。

sentences.en: It's not a man's place to give advice here.
sentences.zh: 这里不是男人给建议的地方。

sentences.en: And she does write something down.
sentences.zh: 于是她写了一些东西。

sentences.en: And she says, I felt a sudden sweat break out all over me.
sentences.zh: 她说，我感到全身突然冒出一阵冷汗。

sentences.en: But then she praises herself, because she's very full of herself, isn't she?
sentences.zh: 但随后她又自我吹捧了一番，因为她非常自负，不是吗？

sentences.en: She says, I do think, though, that the poem of mine isn't the sort of thing that a young person could have come up with.
sentences.zh: 她说，不过，我确实认为我写的这首诗不是年轻人能写出来的。

sentences.en: She's very proud of herself.
sentences.zh: 她对自己非常自豪。

sentences.en: You get this sort of sense of, this really, this would taint her.
sentences.zh: 你会有这种感觉，这真的会玷污她。

sentences.en: People would laugh at her for years.
sentences.zh: 人们会嘲笑她好几年。

sentences.en: You know, when you're at the top, every slip will be fatal, because there are lots of people who want to replace her as the, you know, the queen.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你处于顶峰时，任何一次失误都可能是致命的，因为有很多人想取代她成为，你知道，女王。

sentences.en: Well, not the queen, I mean, but the queen bee, perhaps, among the ladies-in-waiting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不是女王，我的意思是，也许是女官中的“蜂王”。

sentences.en: And a further cause of anxiety is it's not enough just to compose it, but you have to write it, as implied in the passage that you quoted.
sentences.zh: 另一个焦虑的来源是，仅仅创作出来还不够，你还必须把它写出来，正如你引用的段落所暗示的那样。

sentences.en: And writing, calligraphy, is also a crucial part of establishing yourself as civilized.
sentences.zh: 而书写，即书法，也是确立你文明身份的关键部分。

sentences.en: So Genji, for instance, in Murasaki's novel, takes for granted that calligraphy is the surest window into a person's soul that you can possibly find.
sentences.zh: 所以，例如在紫式部的小说中，源氏认为书法是了解一个人灵魂最可靠的窗口。

sentences.en: And that beautiful writing equates to a kind of moral beauty.
sentences.zh: 而优美的书法等同于一种道德上的美。

sentences.en: And there's a whole chapter in the tale of Genji where he and his mates just sit around and talk about calligraphy.
sentences.zh: 《源氏物语》中有一整章，他和他的朋友们就坐在一起谈论书法。

sentences.en: Like it's the, I mean, for them, it is one of the most important things in the world.
sentences.zh: 就像它是，我的意思是，对他们来说，这是世界上最重要的事情之一。

sentences.en: And they agree, everything is going to the dogs except for calligraphy, which has hugely improved.
sentences.zh: 他们一致认为，除了书法大有长进之外，其他一切都在走下坡路。

sentences.en: And Seishonigan, likewise, I mean, it's often features in the list of things that she loves.
sentences.zh: 清少纳言也一样，我的意思是，这经常出现在她所喜爱的事物清单中。

sentences.en: So things that make you feel cheerful, something written in very delicate strokes with just the tip of an almost impossibly thick brush on a lovely,
sentences.zh: 所以那些让你感到愉悦的事情，用几乎不可能那么粗的笔尖，在精美的、

sentences.en: clean white sheet of Michinoku paper.
sentences.zh: 干净洁白的陆奥纸上，写下非常细腻的笔触。

sentences.en: I mean, we're a long way from the Anglo-Saxon court there, I think.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得我们离盎格鲁-撒克逊宫廷还很远。

sentences.en: And the other thing that makes this, if people are not interested in poetry, I think, well, who cares about a load of poems?
sentences.zh: 另一件事让这个，如果人们对诗歌不感兴趣，我想，好吧，谁在乎一堆诗呢？

sentences.en: To be good at poetry and to be able to write this beautiful kind of calligraphy, this is really important, not just for your social standing, but basically,
sentences.zh: 擅长诗歌并能写出这种优美的书法，这真的很重要，不仅是为了你的社会地位，而且基本上，

sentences.en: if you want to have any sexual or romantic success, you have to be good at this.
sentences.zh: 如果你想在性或浪漫方面取得任何成功，你必须擅长这些。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, it makes thinking up a good chat-up line look, you know, trivial by comparison.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，相比之下，想出一句好的搭讪语看起来就显得微不足道了。

sentences.en: I mean, it's kind of like opening proceedings on social media when you never actually met the person.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这有点像在社交媒体上开启对话，而你从未真正见过那个人。

sentences.en: It's a little bit like that because the poem is seen as your window onto the world.
sentences.zh: 有点像那样，因为诗歌被视为你观察世界的窗口。

sentences.en: An erotic adventure at the court is a crucial part of kind of the broader social dynamics.
sentences.zh: 宫廷里的情色冒险是更广泛社会动态的关键部分。

sentences.en: And it's celebrated by Seishonigan, who, again, seems to have been tremendously good at it.
sentences.zh: 清少纳言对此大加赞赏，她似乎在这方面也非常擅长。

sentences.en: She certainly gives that impression.
sentences.zh: 她确实给人留下了这种印象。

sentences.en: But Murasaki as well, even though in her personal relations, she seems to have been viewed actually as a bit of a prude.
sentences.zh: 但紫式部也是如此，尽管在个人关系上，她似乎被视为一个有点保守的人。

sentences.en: And it reflects the way in which women are given a degree of kind of license that I think in the Muslim or Christian world would have prompted a lot of anxiety on the part of male moralists.
sentences.zh: 这反映了女性获得了一定程度的自由，我认为在穆斯林或基督教世界，这会引起男性道德家们极大的焦虑。

sentences.en: There are absolutely rules.
sentences.zh: 当然是有规则的。

sentences.en: I mean, very strict rules.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，非常严格的规则。

sentences.en: But the whole point is, is that you master the rules and then, you know, all kinds of opportunities open up.
sentences.zh: 但重点是，你掌握了规则，然后，你知道，各种机会就会随之而来。

sentences.en: And that's precisely the thrill and the fun of it.
sentences.zh: 而这正是其中的刺激和乐趣所在。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So for women especially, the reason that you want to be very good at poetry is that you are not supposed to show yourself to men who are courting you.
sentences.zh: 所以对于女性来说，你想要非常擅长诗歌的原因是，你不应该向追求你的男人展示自己。

sentences.en: You stay behind a screen.
sentences.zh: 你待在屏风后面。

sentences.en: And so how then are you meant to establish relations with a man if the man can't actually see you, if you have to stay cloistered away behind a screen?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果男人根本看不见你，如果你必须待在屏风后面，你该如何与男人建立关系呢？

sentences.en: And this is where the poetry comes in.
sentences.zh: 这就是诗歌发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: You kind of exchange verses.
sentences.zh: 你们交换诗句。

sentences.en: And if this goes well and if the man thinks, yeah, that's witty, that's well expressed or whatever, then other markers of taste can be unleashed.
sentences.zh: 如果进展顺利，如果男人觉得，嗯，这很机智，表达得很好之类的，那么其他品味的标志就可以展现出来了。

sentences.en: And this is what Genji is so good at.
sentences.zh: 而这正是源氏如此擅长的地方。

sentences.en: He is, in Murasaki's novel, the absolute master of these kind of arts of courtship.
sentences.zh: 在紫式部的小说中，他是这些求爱艺术的绝对大师。

sentences.en: So poetry comes firSt.
sentences.zh: 所以诗歌是第一位的。

sentences.en: Then you might have incense mixing.
sentences.zh: 然后你可能会有香料调配。

sentences.en: So remember, Genji is perfumed.
sentences.zh: 所以记住，源氏是熏香的。

sentences.en: Seishonagon is very good on how wonderful, beautiful scents are and how awful hideous ones are.
sentences.zh: 清少纳言非常擅长描述美妙的香气是多么美妙，而恶心的香气是多么糟糕。

sentences.en: It's clearly very, very important in the court.
sentences.zh: 这在宫廷里显然非常非常重要。

sentences.en: Calligraphy, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然还有书法。

sentences.en: There's a passage in The Tale of Genji where the war minister literally sobs over Genji's calligraphy.
sentences.zh: 《源氏物语》中有一段，兵部卿亲王看着源氏的书法简直痛哭流涕。

sentences.en: And, you know, you can't kind of imagine, I don't know, Pete Hegseth weeping over J.D.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你无法想象，我不知道，皮特·赫格塞斯会对着J.D.

sentences.en: Vance's handwriting.
sentences.zh: 万斯的笔迹哭泣。

sentences.en: That's such a great image.
sentences.zh: 那真是一个很棒的画面。

sentences.en: It's not going to happen.
sentences.zh: 那是不可能发生的。

sentences.en: And then, of course, there's, you know, the exquisiteness of dress and so on.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有，你知道，服饰的精致等等。

sentences.en: So the woman would wear perhaps very, very long sleeves and she would very decorously allow perhaps just a glimpse from behind the screen.
sentences.zh: 所以女性可能会穿非常非常长的袖子，她会非常端庄地允许从屏风后面露出一瞥。

sentences.en: So it's that kind of thing, you know, a glimpse of ankle.
sentences.zh: 所以就是那种事，你知道，露出一截脚踝。

sentences.en: And in due course, a woman who decides that she is happy to allow a man to pay court to her, this would initiate a series of secret nighttime visits.
sentences.zh: 适时地，一个决定愿意让男人追求她的女性，会开启一系列秘密的夜间访问。

sentences.en: And when I say secret, it's not really secret because there is effectively no privacy in these.
sentences.zh: 当我说是秘密时，其实并不秘密，因为在这些地方实际上没有隐私。

sentences.en: Right, because people would see you coming and going, wouldn't they?
sentences.zh: 没错，因为人们会看到你来来往往，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the screens operate as walls within rooms, but I mean, they're, you know, they're not permanent walls.
sentences.zh: 屏风在房间里充当墙壁，但我的意思是，它们，你知道，它们并不是永久性的墙壁。

sentences.en: So they're ultimately, there isn't really any privacy.
sentences.zh: 所以归根结底，其实并没有什么隐私可言。

sentences.en: And it means that in poetry, in prose, in both The Tale of Genji and The Pillow Book,
sentences.zh: 这意味着在诗歌和散文中，无论是在《源氏物语》还是《枕草子》中，

sentences.en: the coming of dawn is a repeated theme because it's absolutely touched with a sense of the erotic.
sentences.zh: 黎明的到来都是一个反复出现的主题，因为它绝对带有一种情欲的意味。

sentences.en: And Seishenagun is predictably brilliant on it.
sentences.zh: 清少纳言对此的描写一如既往地精彩。

sentences.en: So she writes, summer provides the most delightful setting for a secret assignation.
sentences.zh: 她写道，夏天是幽会最美妙的背景。

sentences.en: The nights are so very short that dawn breaks before you've slept.
sentences.zh: 夜晚如此短暂，还没睡着天就亮了。

sentences.en: Everything has been left open all night and there's a lovely cool feel to the expansive view.
sentences.zh: 整晚窗户都敞开着，开阔的视野里透着一股宜人的凉意。

sentences.en: The lovers still have a little more they must say to each other.
sentences.zh: 恋人们还有些话没说完。

sentences.en: As they sit there murmuring endearments, they're startled into a sudden panicky sensation of exposure by the loud caw of a passing crow.
sentences.zh: 当他们坐在那里低声诉说着爱语时，一只乌鸦飞过发出的响亮叫声，让他们突然陷入了一种惊慌失措的暴露感中。

sentences.en: A delightful moment.
sentences.zh: 真是美妙的时刻。

sentences.en: So there's a lovely section at the beginning of The Pillow Book when she's describing a woman and her lover.
sentences.zh: 《枕草子》开头有一段非常精彩的描写，她描述了一位女子和她的情人。

sentences.en: The lover has just left and another bloke is passing because he's leaving an assignation of his own.
sentences.zh: 情人刚走，另一个男人路过，因为他自己也刚结束了一场幽会。

sentences.en: And he sees through the sort of gap in the screen that she's still lying there on the bed.
sentences.zh: 他透过屏风的缝隙，看到她还躺在床上。

sentences.en: And she kind of knows he can see her.
sentences.zh: 而她似乎也察觉到他能看见自己。

sentences.en: And it's a sort of passage again, you know, your mind explodes trying to think about, you know, somebody at the court of Ethelred the Unready writing this.
sentences.zh: 这又是一个让你思绪万千的片段，你想想看，在埃塞尔雷德二世的宫廷里，竟然有人写出这样的文字。

sentences.en: With such delicacy and such a sort of sense of tenderness and melancholy and erotic feeling and whatnot that's just unimaginable in medieval literature otherwise.
sentences.zh: 那种细腻、那种温柔、忧郁和情欲的感觉，在其他中世纪文学中简直是不可想象的。

sentences.en: It obviously reflects different social, cultural, sexual expectations.
sentences.zh: 这显然反映了不同的社会、文化和性观念。

sentences.en: And Christian Europe is a monogamous culture.
sentences.zh: 基督教欧洲是一种一夫一妻制的文化。

sentences.en: That's not the case in Japan.
sentences.zh: 但在日本并非如此。

sentences.en: So these courtships might lead to marriage or it might lead to a kind of polygamous relationship, a kind of secondary degree of marriage of the kind that Genji is so fond of.
sentences.zh: 所以这些求爱可能通向婚姻，也可能通向某种多偶关系，一种源氏非常喜欢的次要程度的婚姻。

sentences.en: Or it might just be a fling.
sentences.zh: 或者可能只是一段露水情缘。

sentences.en: I mean, it's perfectly fine to just kind of have an affair.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，仅仅是谈场恋爱也是完全可以接受的。

sentences.en: And obviously, women are absolutely not passive actors in this.
sentences.zh: 显然，女性在这其中绝非被动的参与者。

sentences.en: You know, they have to project their erotic appeal as well, which is very difficult when you start behind a screen.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她们也必须展现自己的魅力，这在屏风后面开始时是非常困难的。

sentences.en: So there are certain things that are obviously very important to them.
sentences.zh: 所以有些事情对她们来说显然非常重要。

sentences.en: We touched on one of them already, and that is smell.
sentences.zh: 我们之前已经提到过其中一点，那就是气味。

sentences.en: So it's an abiding theme in the tale of Genji.
sentences.zh: 这是《源氏物语》中一个持久的主题。

sentences.en: Women are worried about that they might be, you know, about their perspiration, that they might be giving off body odour.
sentences.zh: 女性担心她们可能会，你知道，担心自己的汗水，担心自己散发出体味。

sentences.en: Where Seishonagan typically riffs on this.
sentences.zh: 清少纳言通常会对此进行发挥。

sentences.en: I mean, she's kind of original.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她很有独创性。

sentences.en: So she says, you know, it's charming.
sentences.zh: 她说，你知道，这很迷人。

sentences.en: A lightly padded kimono that gives off a faint whiff of perspiration.
sentences.zh: 一件略带汗味的轻薄棉袍。

sentences.en: She thinks that's actually quite erotic for a man.
sentences.zh: 她认为这对男人来说其实相当有情调。

sentences.en: And also she gives advice on, in short, because obviously it's a problem if a man is coming and the woman is behind a screen.
sentences.zh: 而且她还给出了建议，简而言之，因为如果男人来了而女人在屏风后面，这显然是个问题。

sentences.en: How is he to know that the woman is there?
sentences.zh: 他怎么知道女人在里面呢？

sentences.en: I mean, she might have gone to bed or something.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她可能已经睡着了之类的。

sentences.en: So Seishonagan advised, shift slightly to let the rustle of clothes alert him.
sentences.zh: 所以清少纳言建议，稍微挪动一下，让衣服的摩擦声提醒他。

sentences.en: So all these kind of rules that I suppose, you know, are freighted with the erotic.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些规则，我想，都是充满了情欲色彩的。

sentences.en: So they're all covered up, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 所以她们都把自己裹得严严实实的，不是吗？

sentences.en: They're wearing, in fact, in the pillar book, in the Penguin Classics edition, there are pictures because clothes are so important.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在企鹅经典版的《枕草子》里，配有插图，因为服装非常重要。

sentences.en: There are diagrams of how they're wearing these enormous, enormous robes.
sentences.zh: 书里有关于她们如何穿着这些巨大、巨大长袍的图解。

sentences.en: And gowns and mantles and jackets and all kinds.
sentences.zh: 还有礼服、披风、夹克等等各种款式。

sentences.en: And I mean, that's in large part, as we will see in due course, because it's very cold in winter.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如我们稍后会看到的，这在很大程度上是因为冬天非常冷。

sentences.en: But it means that clothing becomes a way, again, like poetry in which they can project their personality.
sentences.zh: 但这确实意味着服装成为了一种方式，就像诗歌一样，她们可以通过它来展现自己的个性。

sentences.en: And so it's not surprising that Seishonagan and Murasaki are obsessed by clothes because the fabric, the cut, the style, the coloring, the pairing of colors.
sentences.zh: 所以清少纳言和紫式部对服装如此痴迷也就不足为奇了，因为面料、剪裁、款式、配色、颜色的搭配。

sentences.en: These are ways in which you can project your personality, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我想，这些都是你可以展现个性的方式。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, Chris Harding in his History of Japan that we were talking about last time makes the point that our concept of fashion does not map onto Japan in this period.
sentences.zh: 嗯，克里斯·哈丁在我们上次谈到的《日本史》中指出，我们对时尚的概念并不适用于那个时期的日本。

sentences.en: Because for them, this is everything, you know, the way you construct your outfit, the choice of colors, the way they match.
sentences.zh: 因为对她们来说，这就是一切，你知道，你构建服装的方式，颜色的选择，它们的搭配方式。

sentences.en: It's much more than an optional extra, than a kind of add-on, than a hobby.
sentences.zh: 这远不止是一个可选项，一个附加品，或者一种爱好。

sentences.en: It's the key to your personality and the way you're perceived in the world.
sentences.zh: 这是你个性的关键，也是你在世界上被感知的方式。

sentences.en: And I think also the Japanese understanding of what makes a woman physically attractive is very different.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为日本人对女性身体吸引力的理解也非常不同。

sentences.en: So, obviously, if the courtship goes well, the key moment comes where a woman has to reveal herself.
sentences.zh: 所以，显然，如果求爱顺利，关键时刻就到了，女人必须展现自己。

sentences.en: The man hasn't seen her until this point.
sentences.zh: 男人在此之前还没见过她。

sentences.en: And there are very distinctive standards of beauty.
sentences.zh: 而且有着非常独特的审美标准。

sentences.en: So, teeth have to be black.
sentences.zh: 比如，牙齿必须是黑色的。

sentences.en: And this is a kind of recurrent theme throughout the tale of Genji.
sentences.zh: 这是贯穿《源氏物语》的一个反复出现的主题。

sentences.en: Women blackening their teeth.
sentences.zh: 女性把牙齿染黑。

sentences.en: Eyebrows are plucked and then painted back on.
sentences.zh: 眉毛要拔掉，然后再画上去。

sentences.en: And you have to have a degree of plumpness, I think.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为你必须要有一定的丰腴感。

sentences.en: If you're thin, this is viewed as very, very erotically off-putting.
sentences.zh: 如果你很瘦，这被认为是非常、非常令人倒胃口的。

sentences.en: And there's a sense, I think, almost in which the naked body is seen as unattractive.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，在某种程度上，赤裸的身体被视为没有吸引力。

sentences.en: So, Murasaki writes, the naked body is unforgettably repulsive.
sentences.zh: 所以，紫式部写道，赤裸的身体令人难忘地厌恶。

sentences.en: It really does not have the slightest charm.
sentences.zh: 它确实没有任何魅力可言。

sentences.en: So, this is not a society in which nakedness is seen as something appealing in any way.
sentences.zh: 所以，这不是一个将裸体视为任何吸引人的社会。

sentences.en: And the real obsession is with hair.
sentences.zh: 而真正的痴迷在于头发。

sentences.en: And the longer it is, the smoother, the glossier, the better.
sentences.zh: 越长、越顺滑、越有光泽越好。

sentences.en: And again and again in the tale of Genji.
sentences.zh: 在《源氏物语》中一遍又一遍地出现。

sentences.en: I mean, Genji only has to see a glimpse of hair and he's off.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，源氏只要瞥见一眼头发，他就按捺不住了。

sentences.en: He's unleashed.
sentences.zh: 他被释放了。

sentences.en: And in fact, what he will do, the moment he gets a glimpse of hair, that's when he will start writing his poeMs.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他会做的是，一旦瞥见头发，那就是他开始写诗的时候。

sentences.en: You know, he'll start kind of pestering the woman with his poetry.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他会开始用诗歌纠缠那个女人。

sentences.en: And it's hard to think, you know, of another culture in which the literary and the erotic are so interfused.
sentences.zh: 很难想到还有哪种文化中，文学和情欲结合得如此紧密。

sentences.en: And I think that's a crucial part of explaining why the writings of women in this period are so potent in their effect and so admired by men as well as by women.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是解释为什么这一时期的女性作品如此有影响力，并受到男性和女性共同推崇的关键部分。

sentences.en: There's another woman, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 还有另一位女性，不是吗？

sentences.en: There's another poet called Izumi Shikibu.
sentences.zh: 还有一位诗人叫和泉式部。

sentences.en: And she was a contemporary of these two characters, Murasaki and Sei Shonagon.
sentences.zh: 她是那两位人物，紫式部和清少纳言的同时代人。

sentences.en: And she was a great femme fatale.
sentences.zh: 她是一位伟大的蛇蝎美人。

sentences.en: And she kind of slept around the court and everybody thought, you know, she was a folk hero in the right word.
sentences.zh: 她在宫廷里到处留情，每个人都认为，你知道，用“民间英雄”这个词来形容她是否合适。

sentences.en: She's celebrated as the greatest poet of her period.
sentences.zh: 她被誉为那个时代最伟大的诗人。

sentences.en: And the sense that she is a femme fatale is a crucial part of that.
sentences.zh: 而她作为蛇蝎美人的感觉是其中的关键部分。

sentences.en: So over the course of her life, she burns her way through two husbands, numerous lovers.
sentences.zh: 在她的一生中，她经历了两位丈夫和无数的情人。

sentences.en: Two of these lovers are royal brothers who succeed each other in turn and both in turn then die.
sentences.zh: 其中两位情人是皇室兄弟，他们先后继位，又先后去世。

sentences.en: So there's a slight quality of the vamp to Izumi Shikibu.
sentences.zh: 所以和泉式部身上带有一点妖女的特质。

sentences.en: And it's a measure of, you know, her kind of glamour that within only a few generations, people are writing novels about her.
sentences.zh: 这衡量了，你知道，她那种魅力，仅仅几代人之后，人们就开始写关于她的小说了。

sentences.en: And it's a measure, too, of the high premium that is set on literary genius that her scandalous reputation never threatens her reputation as a great writer.
sentences.zh: 这也衡量了对文学天才的高度重视，她那丑闻般的名声从未威胁到她作为伟大作家的声誉。

sentences.en: In fact, just the opposite.
sentences.zh: 事实上，恰恰相反。
