sentences.en: she places the pillow book in the context of a political crisis at court that was directly threatening, say, Shonakan's position there and the empress that she was serving.
sentences.zh: 她将《枕草子》置于宫廷政治危机的背景下，这场危机直接威胁到清少纳言的地位以及她所服务的皇后。

sentences.en: And so Meredith McKinney describes the pillow book as a work that not only resolutely refuses to acknowledge these sorrows,
sentences.zh: 因此，梅雷迪思·麦金尼将《枕草子》描述为一部不仅坚决拒绝承认这些悲伤的作品，

sentences.en: but that largely refuses to acknowledge sorrow itself and gives us in its place a world of exquisite delight.
sentences.zh: 而且在很大程度上拒绝承认悲伤本身，取而代之的是一个精致愉悦的世界。

sentences.en: And it'll sound a weird parallel, but I thought of P.G.
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能是一个奇怪的类比，但我想到了P.G.伍德豪斯在30年代写的伯蒂·伍斯特，这个充满温和幽默的世界对于萧条、战争之类的东西确实没有容身之地。

sentences.en: Woodhouse writing Bertie Worcester in the 30s, that this world of kind of genial humour has no place really for depressions or wars or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我认为《枕草子》也是如此。

sentences.en: And I think it's similar with the pillow book.
sentences.zh: 这是一种不承认黑暗的刻意决心。

sentences.en: It is a deliberate determination not to admit the darkness.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，一部极其精致和阳光的作品，依赖于一个更加黑暗和充满冲突的背景。

sentences.en: So in other words, a work of great sophistication and sunniness depends on a context that is much darker and more conflicted.
sentences.zh: 那么告诉我们关于这场宫廷危机的事，因为实际上我们一直在谈论的两个角色，紫式部和清少纳言，

sentences.en: So tell us about this crisis at court, because actually the two characters we've been talking about, Murasaki on one side and Seishonagon on the other,
sentences.zh: 她们处于这场略带《权力的游戏》风格的派系斗争的对立面，不是吗？

sentences.en: they are on opposite sides of this slightly Game of Thrones-ish factional battle, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 这在《源氏物语》的第一句话中就有暗示，你在上一集读过。

sentences.en: And it's hinted in the very first sentence of the tale of Genji, which you read out in the previous episode.
sentences.zh: 人们可能还记得。

sentences.en: And people may remember it.
sentences.zh: 开头是：在某个朝代，会是谁的朝代呢？

sentences.en: It starts, In a certain reign, whose can it have been?
sentences.zh: 这引入了一个贯穿全书的主题，即天皇本人是匿名且被动的。

sentences.en: And this introduces a theme that runs throughout the novel, which is that the figure of the emperor himself is kind of anonymous and passive.
sentences.zh: 他们总是被退位并被另一个取代。

sentences.en: And they're always kind of being retired and replaced by another one.
sentences.zh: 他们没有真正的个性。

sentences.en: And they have no real personality.
sentences.zh: 这反映了一个事实，即当桓武天皇时，听过上一集的人可能记得他曾在一个叫奈良的首都，并感到他，

sentences.en: And this reflects the fact that when the emperor Kanmu, people who listened to the last episode may remember that he had been in a capital called Nara and had felt that he,
sentences.zh: 作为天皇，正受到日本大领主们的阴影笼罩。

sentences.en: as emperor, was coming under the shadow of the great lords of Japan.
sentences.zh: 于是他离开并建立了平安京，试图恢复皇权。

sentences.en: And he had gone off and founded Heian Kiyo in an attempt to restore imperial authority.
sentences.zh: 这表明这种努力并没有奏效，在平安京建立后的10世纪期间，

sentences.en: What this suggests is that that effort hadn't worked, that over the course of the 10th century, following the foundation of Heian Kiyo,
sentences.zh: 天皇的权力继续被蚕食。

sentences.en: the emperor had continued to be leeched of his power.
sentences.zh: 虽然他仍然是政府和国家的中心，但这并不是以任何积极的意义。

sentences.en: And although he remains the center of the government and the state, it's not in kind of any active sense.
sentences.zh: 所以他采用了中国的头衔“天子”，我们可以翻译为皇帝。

sentences.en: So he has taken on the Chinese title, Tenu, which we might translate as emperor.
sentences.zh: 而“天子”，我们在上一集说过，意味着北极星。

sentences.en: And Tenu, we said this in the previous episode, means the pole star.
sentences.zh: 正如约书亚·弗里德曼在他关于日本神话的书中所言，北极星什么都不做。

sentences.en: And as Joshua Friedman in his book on Japanese mythology puts it, the pole star does not do anything.
sentences.zh: 它只是坐着。

sentences.en: It simply sits.
sentences.zh: 凭借其存在本身，其他一切都围绕着它旋转。

sentences.en: And by virtue of what it is, everything else rotates around it.
sentences.zh: 理论上“天子”也是一样。

sentences.en: The Tenu is theoretically the same.
sentences.zh: 他存在于政府的中心，万物都围绕着他运行。

sentences.en: He exists at the center of the government and all things orbit around him.
sentences.zh: 但他自己除了存在之外，不需要做任何事情。

sentences.en: But he himself does not need to do anything other than simply be.
sentences.zh: 还有一个词被用来称呼天皇，也可以翻译为皇帝，那就是“帝”，就像吉尔伯特和萨利文的歌剧一样。

sentences.en: And there's another word that is applied to the emperor, which could be translated as emperor, which is Mikado, as in Gilbert and Sullivan opera.
sentences.zh: 这有点像法老。

sentences.en: And this is a bit like Pharaoh.
sentences.zh: 所以法老字面意思是“大房子”。

sentences.en: So Pharaoh means literally the great house.
sentences.zh: 它将统治者与他居住的建筑联系在一起。

sentences.en: It's identifying the figure of the ruler with the architecture of where he lives.
sentences.zh: 而“帝”字面意思是“内宫之门”。

sentences.en: And Mikado literally means gates of the inner palace.
sentences.zh: 这些门把人们挡在外面，但也把天皇关在里面。

sentences.en: And these are the gates that keep the people out, but keep the emperor in.
sentences.zh: 所以，这再次体现了他被关起来的想法。

sentences.en: So, again, it's this idea that he's being kind of closeted away.
sentences.zh: 他就像系统核心的一名囚犯。

sentences.en: He's like a prisoner at the heart of the system.
sentences.zh: 是的，差不多。

sentences.en: Yeah, almoSt.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，当你去东京时，皇宫还有这道令人惊叹的护城河。

sentences.en: And when you go to Tokyo to this day, the palace has this amazing moat.
sentences.zh: 它有这些巨大的围墙。

sentences.en: It has these great walls.
sentences.zh: 你看不见里面。

sentences.en: You can't see inside.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，天皇感觉像是一个非常隐形的中心，我想即使在11世纪也是如此。

sentences.en: I mean, the emperor feels a kind of very invisible center, which I guess is what he is even back in the 11th century.
sentences.zh: 所以如果天皇不是真的，你知道，他不是独裁者。

sentences.en: So if the emperor is not really, you know, he's not the autocrat.
sentences.zh: 他没有管理国家。

sentences.en: He's not running the state.
sentences.zh: 谁在管理国家？

sentences.en: Who is running the state?
sentences.zh: 因为我们还没有进入幕府时代，你知道，那些伟大的军阀。

sentences.en: Because we're not yet in the age of the shogun, you know, the great warlords.
sentences.zh: 武士和伟大的封建竞争。

sentences.en: The samurai and the great feudal rivalries.
sentences.zh: 那么谁在负责？

sentences.en: So who's in charge?
sentences.zh: 在我们谈论的那个时代，基本上是一个家族，藤原氏。

sentences.en: At the time we've been talking about, it's basically a single family, the Fujiwara.
sentences.zh: 他们非常古老，非常显赫。

sentences.en: And they are very ancient, very distinguished.
sentences.zh: 所以即使在奈良时代，随着那里的所有派系斗争，他们也一直是主要参与者。

sentences.en: So even back in the time of Nara, with all the faction fighting there, they had been kind of leading players.
sentences.zh: 但到了10世纪中叶，他们实际上已经确立了自己作为宫廷统治者的地位，因此，推而广之，也就是整个日本的统治者。

sentences.en: But by the middle of the 10th century, they've effectively established themselves as the rulers of the court and therefore, by extension, the whole of Japan.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做并不是靠炫耀武力。

sentences.en: And they do this not by kind of throwing their weight around.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们没有随叫随到的武士。

sentences.en: You know, they don't have samurai at their beck and call.
sentences.zh: 他们不是伟大的军事领袖。

sentences.en: They're not great military leaders.
sentences.zh: 他们之所以能做到这一点，是因为他们精通政治和派系斗争，特别是日本历史学家所说的“婚姻政治”。

sentences.en: They do it because they are brilliant at politics and at faction fighting and specifically at what Japanese historians call marriage politics.
sentences.zh: 婚姻政治的精髓就是让天皇娶你的女儿，这样你就能与坐在王位上的人结成姻亲。

sentences.en: And the essence of marriage politics is to get the emperor married to your daughter so that you will be related by marriage to the figure who sits on the throne.
sentences.zh: 所以，引用伊万·莫里斯的话，

sentences.en: So, to quote Ivan Morris,
sentences.zh: 到了10世纪，藤原氏强加给天皇一种几乎注定要让他处于家族控制之下的生命周期。

sentences.en: By the 10th century, the Fujiwaras had imposed on the emperor a type of life cycle that was almost bound to keep him under the family's thumb.
sentences.zh: 他以一个毛头小子的身份登上王位，并立即被安排娶了一位藤原家的女孩。

sentences.en: He came to the throne as a callow youth and was promptly married to a Fujiwara girl.
sentences.zh: 他们的儿子将被任命为皇太子。

sentences.en: Their son would be appointed crown prince.
sentences.zh: 他们的儿子将被任命为皇太子。

sentences.en: And when his father was obliged to abdicate, usually at the age of about 30, this crown prince would succeed him and the cycle would start again.
sentences.zh: 当皇太子年满三十岁左右，其父通常会被迫退位，皇太子继位，循环往复。

sentences.en: So, there's no way for the emperor to break free of the kind of marriage chains that the Fujiwaras are fettering them with.
sentences.zh: 因此，天皇根本无法摆脱藤原氏施加的婚姻枷锁。

sentences.en: And the effective ruler of Japan, when, say, Shonagon comes to court, is a man who by now is not unofficial.
sentences.zh: 当清少纳言入宫时，日本的实际统治者已经不再是幕后人物了。

sentences.en: It's formal.
sentences.zh: 他是名正言顺的。

sentences.en: He is ruling as the regent for the emperor.
sentences.zh: 他以摄政的身份统治着天皇。

sentences.en: And he's done this by marrying his daughter, who is a woman called Teishi, to the emperor Ichijo, who is only 11 years old.
sentences.zh: 他通过将自己的女儿定子嫁给年仅十一岁的一条天皇，实现了这一点。

sentences.en: So, very, very, you know, easy to be manipulated.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他非常、非常容易被操纵。

sentences.en: And Ichijo is always under Michitaka's thumb, partly because he's a boy, partly because there are three retired emperors on the scene.
sentences.zh: 一条天皇一直处于藤原道隆的掌控之下，部分原因是他年纪尚小，另一部分原因是当时还有三位退位的天皇在场。

sentences.en: You know, they've all been kind of, you know, retired off.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们都算是被“退休”了。

sentences.en: So, that dilutes his authority, obviously.
sentences.zh: 显然，这削弱了他的权威。

sentences.en: And I think partly because he's raised and educated never to oppose the Fujiwara.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，部分原因是他从小受到的教育就是绝不能反抗藤原氏。

sentences.en: He just sits in his palace and, you know, plays his former role.
sentences.zh: 他只是坐在宫中，你知道，扮演着他原有的角色。

sentences.en: And that's it.
sentences.zh: 仅此而已。

sentences.en: And so, Teishi, his wife, she is the empress for whom Sei Shonagon, whom she served.
sentences.zh: 定子皇后就是清少纳言所侍奉的那位皇后。

sentences.en: And the one who got Sei Shonagon to write all his poems and, you know, had the bet with her about the snow and all that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 正是她让清少纳言写下了那些诗句，还和她打赌关于雪之类的事情。

sentences.en: And Sei Shonagon thinks Teishi is great.
sentences.zh: 清少纳言认为定子非常了不起。

sentences.en: You know, she thinks she's funny, she's smart, she's stylish.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她觉得定子风趣、聪明、时髦。

sentences.en: And in exchange, the presence of Sei Shonagon at Teishi's side as part of her retinue adds greatly to Teishi's prestige because Sei Shonagon is that famous, that celebrated.
sentences.zh: 作为回报，清少纳言作为定子随从出现在她身边，极大地提升了定子的声望，因为清少纳言是如此出名、如此受人赞誉。

sentences.en: But obviously, the position of both women is kind of precarious.
sentences.zh: 但显然，这两位女性的处境都有些岌岌可危。

sentences.en: I mean, both of them are completely aware of this because it depends on Michitaka remaining on the scene and keeping hold of power.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她们俩都完全意识到了这一点，因为这取决于道隆能否留在朝中并掌握权力。

sentences.en: And I think despite the pretty consistent tone of sunniness and lightness that you get in the pillow book,
sentences.zh: 我认为，尽管《枕草子》中始终贯穿着一种阳光明媚、轻松愉快的基调，

sentences.en: occasionally there's the odd hint from Sei Shonagon that she is aware of this.
sentences.zh: 但清少纳言偶尔也会流露出她对此有所察觉的迹象。

sentences.en: It's a little bit like the black shorts in Bertie Worcester.
sentences.zh: 这有点像伯蒂·伍斯特故事里的黑色短裤。

sentences.en: There's kind of a little hint of the darkness off stage.
sentences.zh: 舞台之外有一种隐约的黑暗气息。

sentences.en: So there's a scene where Sei Shonagon describes Michitaka.
sentences.zh: 书中有一段清少纳言描写道隆的场景。

sentences.en: She thinks he's great, looking wonderfully slender and elegant, pausing to adjust his ceremonial sword.
sentences.zh: 她觉得他很棒，身形修长优雅，停下来整理佩剑的样子令人赞叹。

sentences.en: And then she describes how Michitaka's brother, the commissioner Michinaga, did not just bow before his brother, but sank to his knees.
sentences.zh: 然后她描述了道隆的弟弟、内大臣道长不仅向兄长鞠躬，甚至跪倒在地的情景。

sentences.en: And she goes and relates to Teishi what she's seen and says, oh, it's marvellous, such a beautiful scene.
sentences.zh: 她跑去向定子讲述了她所见的一切，说，哦，太棒了，真是美丽的场景。

sentences.en: And then she writes, when I kept mentioning to Her Majesty how Commissioner Michinaga, so the younger brother, had bowed before the region,
sentences.zh: 然后她写道，当我不断向皇后提起内大臣道长——也就是那位弟弟——是如何在摄政面前鞠躬时，

sentences.en: she smilingly teased me by referring to him as that perennial favourite of yours.
sentences.zh: 她微笑着打趣我，称他为“你那位长盛不衰的宠儿”。

sentences.en: If she could have lived to witness the greatness he later attained, she would have realised how right I was to find him so impressive.
sentences.zh: 如果她能活到见证他后来取得的伟大成就，她就会明白我当时为何对他印象如此深刻。

sentences.en: So she's writing at a time where Teishi has died and where Michinaga has replaced Michitaka as regent.
sentences.zh: 所以她写作时，定子已经去世，道长也已经取代道隆成为了摄政。

sentences.en: And that happened in, so Michitaka died in 995.
sentences.zh: 那发生在九九五年，道隆在那一年去世。

sentences.en: And what happens then is that the next brother in line succeeds Michitaka, dies within a few days.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的事是，排在下一位的兄弟继任了道隆，但没过几天就去世了。

sentences.en: And so Michinaga then becomes regent.
sentences.zh: 于是道长便成为了摄政。

sentences.en: And for Teishi and Seishonagon, this is very bad news, because obviously Michinaga is going to want to marry one of his own daughters to the emperor, Ichijo.
sentences.zh: 对于定子和清少纳言来说，这可是个坏消息，因为显然道长会想把自己的女儿嫁给一条天皇。

sentences.en: Oh, right.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.en: OK, so the fact that it's his niece, it's his niece, right?
sentences.zh: 好吧，他是他侄女的父亲，对吧？

sentences.en: That's not good enough.
sentences.zh: 那还不够好。

sentences.en: It's got to be his daughter.
sentences.zh: 必须得是他自己的女儿。

sentences.en: He's not going to bump Teishi off.
sentences.zh: 他不会除掉定子。

sentences.en: He's not going to set her aside.
sentences.zh: 他不会废黜她。

sentences.en: But what he is going to do is essentially ensure that there is a second empress.
sentences.zh: 但他要做的是确保出现第二位皇后。

sentences.en: So there will be two empresses of equal rank.
sentences.zh: 这样就会有两位地位相当的皇后。

sentences.en: But this obviously destabilizes Teishi's position massively.
sentences.zh: 但这显然极大地动摇了定子的地位。

sentences.en: And it happens in the year 1000.
sentences.zh: 这发生在公元一千年。

sentences.en: So Michinaga has a 10-year-old daughter called Shoshi, and she gets married to the emperor.
sentences.zh: 道长有一个十岁的女儿叫彰子，她嫁给了天皇。

sentences.en: And there are now two empresses, and there are two courts.
sentences.zh: 现在有了两位皇后，也就有了两个宫廷。

sentences.en: And Michinaga obviously knows Seishonagon well.
sentences.zh: 道长显然很了解清少纳言。

sentences.en: You know, they've been kind of bantering, and Seishonagon's been going on about how brilliant he is when he kneels before his brother and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们之间有过调侃，清少纳言一直在说当他跪在兄长面前时他是多么出色之类的话。

sentences.en: And he basically wants his daughter, Shoshi, to have a literary superstar as a lady-in-waiting as well.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是想让他的女儿彰子也拥有一位文学巨星作为女官。

sentences.en: And this is where Murasaki Shikabu comes in, because she is not just celebrated for her learning and her literary genius,
sentences.zh: 这就是紫式部登场的原因，因为她不仅以学识和文学天才而闻名，

sentences.en: but she's actually a Fujiwara herself, albeit from quite a kind of minor branch of the family.
sentences.zh: 而且她本人也是藤原氏，尽管是家族中相当旁支的一脉。

sentences.en: So she's perfect.
sentences.zh: 所以她是完美的人选。

sentences.en: So Murasaki comes in, and you can see why this would add an extra dimension to the rivalry between the two women.
sentences.zh: 于是紫式部入宫了，你可以看出为什么这会给两位女性之间的竞争增加额外的维度。

sentences.en: And it's Murasaki, it turns out, basically, who has backed the winning side.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，基本上是紫式部押注了获胜的一方。

sentences.en: Because a few months after Shoshi has been promoted to the rank of joint empress alongside Teishi, so marrying Ichijo, Teishi dies in childbirth.
sentences.zh: 因为在彰子被提升为与定子并列的皇后几个月后，也就是嫁给一条天皇之后，定子在分娩时去世了。

sentences.en: And so all eyes now are on Shoshi.
sentences.zh: 所以现在所有的目光都集中在彰子身上。

sentences.en: Will she be able to give her husband a son and thereby ensure her father's hold on power?
sentences.zh: 她能否为丈夫生下一个儿子，从而确保她父亲对权力的掌控？

sentences.en: She's only 10 when she marries.
sentences.zh: 她结婚时才十岁。

sentences.en: It's eight years before she finally gets pregnant.
sentences.zh: 过了八年她才终于怀孕。

sentences.en: And then again, there's massive tension, because will she survive childbirth?
sentences.zh: 然后，又是一阵巨大的紧张，因为她能挺过分娩吗？

sentences.en: And if she does, will she deliver a boy?
sentences.zh: 如果她挺过来了，她能生个男孩吗？

sentences.en: And it's amid this mood of tension that Murasaki begins her diary.
sentences.zh: 正是在这种紧张的气氛中，紫式部开始写她的日记。

sentences.en: I mean, it's an incredibly dramatic moment.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个极其戏剧性的时刻。

sentences.en: And so she describes Her Majesty listens to her ladies-in-waiting engaged in idle gossip.
sentences.zh: 她描述了皇后听着女官们闲聊的情景。

sentences.en: She must be in some distress.
sentences.zh: 她一定感到非常痛苦。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太惊人了。

sentences.en: It's an account of an event that is so important in monarchies throughout history and across the world.
sentences.zh: 这是对历史上世界各地君主制中都极其重要的一件事的记录。

sentences.en: Will the wife of a ruler give that ruler a son?
sentences.zh: 统治者的妻子会为他生下一个儿子吗？

sentences.en: And here you have one of the greatest writers of all time describing it in journalistic fashion.
sentences.zh: 而在这里，你有一位史上最伟大的作家以新闻报道的方式描述了它。

sentences.en: Yeah, as though it's in real time.
sentences.zh: 是的，就像是实时发生的一样。

sentences.en: And big spoiler alert, Shoshi does survive childbirth, and she does have a son, which is brilliant for Michinaga, because his power base is now secure.
sentences.zh: 剧透预警，彰子确实挺过了分娩，并且生下了一个儿子，这对道长来说太棒了，因为他的权力基础现在稳固了。

sentences.en: Yeah, and so he stays securely in power until he dies in 1028, and no one thinks to challenge him.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以他稳稳地掌握着权力直到一零二八年去世，没有人想挑战他。

sentences.en: And by the time he dies, he has been brother-in-law to two emperors, uncle to one, uncle and father-in-law to Ichijo, so that's another one, and grandfather to two more emperors.
sentences.zh: 到他去世时，他已经是两位天皇的姐夫/妹夫，一位天皇的舅舅，一条天皇的舅舅兼岳父，以及另外两位天皇的祖父。

sentences.en: So, I mean, he is absolutely at the center of power in the imperial palace.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，他绝对处于皇宫权力的中心。

sentences.en: For Seishonigan and Murasaki Shikibu, for the former, the death of Teishi spells the end of her time at court.
sentences.zh: 对于清少纳言和紫式部来说，对于前者，定子的死意味着她在宫廷时光的终结。

sentences.en: And so you can see, I think, therefore, that the Pillow book, much of which she must have written in retirement, actually there is,
sentences.zh: 所以我想你可以看出，《枕草子》的大部分内容一定是她在隐居时写的，实际上，

sentences.en: it is written with a real consciousness of bereavement, almoSt.
sentences.zh: 它写的时候带有一种真正的丧亲意识，几乎是这样。

sentences.en: And, you know, and if it's a eulogy to joy, which it undoubtedly is, it's one of the most joyous books you could possibly read, I think it is also testimony to the fleeting nature,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，如果这是一首对快乐的颂歌——它无疑是，我认为它是你能读到的最快乐的书之一——它也证明了快乐的短暂性，

sentences.en: the insubstantiality of joy.
sentences.zh: 快乐的虚幻性。

sentences.en: Murasaki, I mean, she seems to have come out as a winner,
sentences.zh: 紫式部，我的意思是，她似乎成了赢家，

sentences.en: so she ends up so close to Michinaga that there are all kinds of far-fetched stories told in the decades and centuries that follow that she'd actually had a relationship with him.
sentences.zh: 她最终与道长走得如此之近，以至于在随后的几十年和几个世纪里，流传着各种牵强附会的故事，说她实际上与他有过一段情。

sentences.en: And I think there's no doubt that Genji as a character and his rise to greatness is kind of modelled a bit on Michinaga.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为毫无疑问，源氏这个角色及其走向伟大的历程在某种程度上是以道长为原型的。

sentences.en: And Ichijo, he loves stories, and so he loves the tale of Genji.
sentences.zh: 一条天皇喜欢故事，所以他喜欢《源氏物语》。

sentences.en: And it may well be that it's this that encourages Murasaki to write it at the length that she does.
sentences.zh: 很可能正是这一点鼓励紫式部写出了如此篇幅的作品。

sentences.en: And, of course, Michinaga is delighted about this because it intensifies Ichijo's devotion to Shoshi, to Michinaga's daughter.
sentences.zh: 当然，道长对此感到非常高兴，因为它加强了一条天皇对彰子——也就是道长女儿——的爱慕。

sentences.en: So you can see the way in which literature isn't at a remove from power politics, but is absolutely kind of woven into it.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看出文学并不是远离权力政治，而是完全融入其中。

sentences.en: You know, does this make Murasaki happy?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这让紫式部感到快乐吗？

sentences.en: I don't think she's a particularly happy person.
sentences.zh: 我不认为她是一个特别快乐的人。

sentences.en: And much more readily than, say, Shonagon is in her diary, but even more so and more powerfully in the tale of Genji,
sentences.zh: 比起清少纳言在日记中的表现，甚至在《源氏物语》中表现得更为强烈和有力，

sentences.en: the fleeting nature of joy and the pain that you can feel in recalling moments of joy is kind of one of her great themes.
sentences.zh: 快乐的短暂性以及回忆快乐时刻时所能感受到的痛苦，是她的一大主题。

sentences.en: There's a famous scene, isn't there, later in the book when Genji meets – he's old at this point.
sentences.zh: 书中后段有一个著名的场景，不是吗？源氏当时已经老了。

sentences.en: He meets a woman that he'd been in love with for many years, and he writes her a poem, very sort of,
sentences.zh: 他遇到了一个他爱慕多年的女人，他写给她一首诗，非常……

sentences.en: Who else but we too knows all that has brought us here, and so may address the pines of Sumiyoshi, witness to the god's own time.
sentences.zh: “除了我们俩，谁还知道这一切是如何将我们带到这里的，所以可以向住吉的松树倾诉，见证神灵的时代。”

sentences.en: So what does that draw on, Tom?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这借鉴了什么？

sentences.en: Well, there are lines that are drawing, I guess, on the kind of the primal beliefs of Japan, the Shinto beliefs.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想这些诗句借鉴了日本原始的信仰，即神道教信仰。

sentences.en: So you have pines that are so ancient that, like so much of the natural world, whether it's rivers or mountains or whatever, that they must be held divine.
sentences.zh: 所以你有那些古老的松树，就像自然界中的许多事物一样，无论是河流、山脉还是其他什么，它们一定被视为神圣的。

sentences.en: You have the god's own time, which equates to eternity, and therefore you have a sense that love itself can cheat time.
sentences.zh: 你有“神灵的时代”，这等同于永恒，因此你有一种感觉，爱本身可以欺骗时间。

sentences.en: But the thing is that even as Genji is composing these lines, he doesn't actually in his heart believe it.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，即使源氏在创作这些诗句时，他内心深处并不真正相信这一点。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is that all the manifestations of Chinese culture that we've been describing,
sentences.zh: 原因在于，我们一直在描述的所有中国文化的表现形式，

sentences.en: the writing, the poetry, the fashions, the song, the dance, the stars of government, these are not the only legacy of that kind of, you know, those centuries of Sinomania,
sentences.zh: 写作、诗歌、时尚、歌舞、政府的星象，这些并不是那几个世纪“中国热”的唯一遗产，

sentences.en: because, and we haven't yet touched really on the sacral, there is another aspect of Chinese culture which takes off in Japan to a momentous degree, and that is Buddhism.
sentences.zh: 因为——我们还没有真正触及神圣领域——中国文化还有另一个方面在日本得到了极大的发展，那就是佛教。

sentences.en: Well, you say the sacral, Tom, but they wouldn't have the, that word would be slightly meaningless to them, wouldn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你说神圣领域，汤姆，但对他们来说这个词会有点毫无意义，不是吗？

sentences.en: It would.
sentences.zh: 确实会。

sentences.en: Because the very idea of religion would be meaningless because there's no distinction between the secular and the religious in Japan.
sentences.zh: 因为宗教的概念本身就是毫无意义的，因为在日本，世俗和宗教之间没有区别。

sentences.en: God Almighty, I'm sounding like Tom Holland.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我听起来像汤姆·霍兰德了。

sentences.en: You are sounding like me.
sentences.zh: 你听起来确实像我。

sentences.en: Yes, you are absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 是的，你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: But let's call it Buddhism, for want of a better word.
sentences.zh: 但为了方便起见，我们还是称之为佛教吧。

sentences.en: And it arrives in Japan, probably in the 6th century.
sentences.zh: 它大概在六世纪传入日本。

sentences.en: It flourishes at Nara in the 8th century.
sentences.zh: 在八世纪的奈良繁荣起来。

sentences.en: Nara boasts the most wonderful Buddhist temples, astonishing statues.
sentences.zh: 奈良拥有最美妙的佛教寺庙和令人惊叹的雕像。

sentences.en: I mean, you're just about to go to Japan, aren't you, I think?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你正准备去日本，对吧？

sentences.en: This will blow people's minds.
sentences.zh: 这会让人大开眼界。

sentences.en: I'm actually going to stay in a Buddhist monastery in Japan.
sentences.zh: 我确实打算在日本的一座佛教寺院里住上一段时间。

sentences.en: Are you going to Nara?
sentences.zh: 你要去奈良吗？

sentences.en: I am going to Nara.
sentences.zh: 我要去奈良。

sentences.en: And it's not in Mara.
sentences.zh: 它不在奈良。

sentences.en: It's on Mount Koya, which is the sacred Buddhist mountain.
sentences.zh: 它在高野山，那是神圣的佛教山脉。

sentences.en: Now, I know this is not part of the persona.
sentences.zh: 现在，我知道这不是（播客）人设的一部分。

sentences.en: And so I hate to tell people this, but our podcast personas are not our entire personalities.
sentences.zh: 我很不想告诉人们这一点，但我们的播客人设并不是我们人格的全部。

sentences.en: It's quite white lotus as well.
sentences.zh: 这也很像《白莲花度假村》。

sentences.en: Well, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: I hope there won't be white lotus style behavior.
sentences.zh: 我希望不会有《白莲花》式的行为。

sentences.en: So Nara is a kind of great Buddhist city.
sentences.zh: 所以奈良是一座伟大的佛教城市。

sentences.en: And that's one of the reasons actually why the capital gets moved is because the monks there are wielding such power that the emperor is feeling in their shadow as well.
sentences.zh: 这也是迁都的原因之一，因为那里的僧侣掌握着巨大的权力，以至于天皇也感到自己处于他们的阴影之下。

sentences.en: And by the 9th century, going into the 10th and 11th century, native and Buddhist traditions are kind of merging to create a definitively Japanese form of Buddhism.
sentences.zh: 到了九世纪，进入十世纪和十一世纪，本土传统和佛教传统开始融合，创造出了一种明确的日本佛教形式。

sentences.en: And this is manifest everywhere in Heian Kyo.
sentences.zh: 这在平安京随处可见。

sentences.en: So that temple bell, which Seishonagun hears ringing in the dead of night when she's tucked up under her bedclothes, that's a Buddhist bell.
sentences.zh: 所以清少纳言在深夜蜷缩在被子里听到的那声寺庙钟声，那是佛教的钟声。

sentences.en: And Murasaki, when she's describing how the emperor Soshi is preparing to give birth to her child, she hears, she describes hearing voices in ceaseless recitation of sutras,
sentences.zh: 而紫式部在描述彰子皇后准备分娩时，她听到、描述了听到不断诵经的声音，

sentences.en: which are the voices of Buddhist monks.
sentences.zh: 那是佛教僧侣的声音。

sentences.en: And there is a town called Uji, which is about 10 miles south of Heian Kyo, where the final chapters of the tale of Genji is set.
sentences.zh: 有一个叫宇治的小镇，在平安京以南约十英里处，《源氏物语》的最后几章就设定在那里。

sentences.en: And Michinaga buys a villa there, which is then converted by his son into a great Buddhist temple.
sentences.zh: 道长在那里买了一座别墅，后来被他的儿子改建成了一座宏伟的佛教寺庙。

sentences.en: This temple appears on one of the Japanese coins.
sentences.zh: 这座寺庙出现在日本的硬币上。

sentences.en: And it contains what is one of the few surviving masterpieces of Heian art, which is this colossal wooden sculpture of the Buddha.
sentences.zh: 它收藏着平安时代艺术中仅存的杰作之一，那就是这尊巨大的木制佛像。

sentences.en: So Buddhism is an absolutely fundamental part of Heian Kyo, this world described by the great writers of the period.
sentences.zh: 所以佛教是平安京的一个绝对基础的部分，也就是那个时代伟大作家所描述的世界。

sentences.en: But if you think of it, you mentioned Shinto before.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想一想，你之前提到了神道教。

sentences.en: These are not competing religions in the sense that we would think of Christianity and Islam or Christianity and paganism, right?
sentences.zh: 这些并不是我们所认为的基督教与伊斯兰教，或者基督教与异教那种相互竞争的宗教，对吧？

sentences.en: They are, even today, lots of Japanese people struggle when they're asked, do you believe in Shintoism or you're a Buddhist?
sentences.zh: 即使在今天，许多日本人在被问到“你信仰神道教还是佛教？”时也会感到困惑。

sentences.en: Because they don't understand the concept that you would be picking and choosing different belief systems entirely.
sentences.zh: 因为他们不理解那种必须完全挑选不同信仰体系的概念。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, it's really striking having written so much about Christianity and its emergence in antiquity and pagan antiquity.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，在写了那么多关于基督教及其在古代和异教古代兴起的内容后，这真的很引人注目。

sentences.en: Buddhism in Japan is such a contraSt.
sentences.zh: 日本的佛教形成了鲜明的对比。

sentences.en: So whereas Christianity banishes the ancient gods of the Mediterranean, that doesn't happen in Japan.
sentences.zh: 所以，虽然基督教驱逐了地中海的古代神灵，但这在日本并没有发生。

sentences.en: I mean, there are definitely tensions.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，肯定存在紧张关系。

sentences.en: There are elements of the kind of the native traditions that really oppose the introduction of Buddhism, but they are not driven out.
sentences.zh: 本土传统中确实有一些因素非常反对佛教的引入，但它们并没有被驱逐出去。

sentences.en: So in the time of Murasaki and, say, Shonagon, the emperor, as the emperor today does, is still claiming descent from the sun goddess.
sentences.zh: 所以在紫式部和清少纳言的时代，天皇——正如今天的天皇一样——仍然声称自己是太阳女神的后裔。

sentences.en: His virgin daughter will be serving as the sun goddess's priestess in what is the greatest shrine in Japan.
sentences.zh: 他未婚的女儿将作为太阳女神的女祭司，在日本最伟大的神社中服务。

sentences.en: And you still have this sense that the divine is imminent in the natural world that was kind of evident in that poem that Genji writes.
sentences.zh: 而且你仍然有一种感觉，神性存在于自然界中，这在源氏写的那首诗中表现得很明显。

sentences.en: But Buddhism, although it is able to coexist with these beliefs, it does teach that the gods worshipped, you know, in these various shrines or whatever,
sentences.zh: 但佛教，尽管它能够与这些信仰共存，它确实教导说，在这些各种神社中崇拜的神灵，无论是什么，

sentences.en: are themselves part of the illusory world, along with the beauties of the natural world, love, the world itself, in fact.
sentences.zh: 它们本身就是虚幻世界的一部分，自然界的美景、爱情，甚至这个世界本身，其实也都是如此。

sentences.en: And this is what everybody that we've been talking about in this episode and the previous episode believes.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我们在本集和上一集中谈到的每个人所相信的。

sentences.en: So Shonagon does.
sentences.zh: 清少纳言也是如此。

sentences.en: And it's said, we don't know with what reliability, but it's often repeated, that at the end of her life, she follows the example of what lots of other people at court,
sentences.zh: 据说——虽然我们不知道其可靠性如何，但这种说法经常被提及——在她生命的尽头，她效仿了宫廷中许多其他人的做法，

sentences.en: including emperors, do, which is to renounce the world.
sentences.zh: 包括天皇在内，那就是遁入空门。

sentences.en: And she throws away her beautiful clothes and she shaves off her beautiful hair and she becomes a nun.
sentences.zh: 她抛弃了华丽的衣裳，剃去了秀发，成为了一名尼姑。

sentences.en: And this is something that Murasaki, we know, was very tempted by.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，紫式部也曾深受此念的诱惑。

sentences.en: Because she feels dread that as a woman, she is fated not to attain enlightenment, that she's bound to be reborn,
sentences.zh: 因为她感到恐惧，作为女性，她注定无法获得觉悟，注定要轮回转世，

sentences.en: that she'll have to be reborn as a man before she can have any prospect of enlightenment.
sentences.zh: 她必须先转世为男人，才有可能获得觉悟。

sentences.en: And she writes about, I think, very painfully and movingly.
sentences.zh: 我想，她对此的描写非常痛苦且动人。

sentences.en: Someone with as much to atone for as myself may not qualify for salvation.
sentences.zh: 像我这样罪孽深重的人，或许没有资格获得救赎。

sentences.en: There are so many things that serve to remind one of the transgressions of a former existence.
sentences.zh: 有太多的事物让人想起前世的罪孽。

sentences.en: Everything conspires to make me unhappy.
sentences.zh: 万事万物都在合谋让我陷入不幸。

sentences.en: And I think it's that capacity to worry that everything that is beautiful and a cause of happiness is itself an illusion that gives the tale of Genji its distinctive character,
sentences.zh: 我认为，正是这种忧虑——即一切美好与快乐的源泉本身都是虚幻的——赋予了《源氏物语》独特的特质，

sentences.en: that it expresses such love for the beauties and joys of the moment.
sentences.zh: 它表达了对当下美好与快乐的深切热爱。

sentences.en: But also such a sense of sorrow that these beauties and joys will ultimately vanish.
sentences.zh: 但也表达了一种深沉的悲哀，因为这些美好与快乐终将消逝。

sentences.en: And in fact, you have to reject them if you are going to attain the eternal beauty and joy of enlightenment.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果你想获得永恒的美好与觉悟，就必须摒弃它们。

sentences.en: And so Murasaki, you know, she says, I want to give it all up.
sentences.zh: 所以紫式部说，我想放弃这一切。

sentences.en: I want to become a nun.
sentences.zh: 我想出家为尼。

sentences.en: But she also dreads it.
sentences.zh: 但她也对此感到恐惧。

sentences.en: And she writes, supposing I were to commit myself and turn my back on the world.
sentences.zh: 她写道：假设我下定决心，背弃这个世界。

sentences.en: I am certain there would be moments of irresolution before a meter came for me riding on his clouds.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定，在阿弥陀佛乘云前来接引我之前，我心中定会有动摇的时刻。

sentences.en: So who is who is a meter?
sentences.zh: 那么，谁是阿弥陀佛？

sentences.en: Is he he's a version of the Buddha?
sentences.zh: 他是佛陀的一种化身吗？

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: So he is a Buddha.
sentences.zh: 是的，他就是一位佛。

sentences.en: He is the Buddha to whom the Hayankorti is seen particularly to have prayed.
sentences.zh: 他正是平安时代人们普遍祈祷的那位佛陀。

sentences.en: So in Uji, this great temple, the great statue carved out of wood and gilded there is a meter.
sentences.zh: 在宇治的那座大寺庙里，那尊巨大的木雕镀金佛像就是阿弥陀佛。

sentences.en: And the appeal of a meter, I think there are there are two aspects to it.
sentences.zh: 我认为阿弥陀佛的吸引力在于两个方面。

sentences.en: The first is that he seems to promise enlightenment to everyone.
sentences.zh: 首先，他似乎向所有人承诺了觉悟。

sentences.en: So this is why he's particularly popular with women.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他特别受女性欢迎。

sentences.en: He seems to offer the promise to women that they don't have to be reborn necessarily.
sentences.zh: 他似乎向女性承诺，她们不必非要经历转世。

sentences.en: But also he seems to promise that love can survive death because what he is supposed to have done is that when he attained enlightenment,
sentences.zh: 但他也似乎承诺了爱情可以超越死亡，因为据传他在获得觉悟时，

sentences.en: the Amida Buddha creates a paradise in the uttermost West and that people who pray to him for salvation can attain this kind of this paradise,
sentences.zh: 阿弥陀佛在极乐西方创造了一个天堂，向他祈求救赎的人可以到达这个天堂，

sentences.en: this Western pure land, and they will be reborn there and they will live in this.
sentences.zh: 即西方净土，他们将在那里重生并生活。

sentences.en: Essentially, it's a kind of paradise that precious metals are living.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，那是一个珍宝遍地的天堂。

sentences.en: Jewels grow from the ground and people themselves, when they are born there, emerge from lotuses into eternal light.
sentences.zh: 珠宝从地里长出来，人们在那里出生时，会从莲花中现身，进入永恒的光明之中。

sentences.en: They're free from any sort of sin and though in due course they will die, then they will attain enlightenment.
sentences.zh: 他们摆脱了一切罪孽，虽然最终也会死去，但那时他们将获得觉悟。

sentences.en: So it's a kind of, it's a final stage, a beautiful final stage before finally attaining the enlightenment that is the desire of every BuddhiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种最终阶段，在最终获得每一位佛教徒所渴望的觉悟之前，这是一个美丽的最终阶段。

sentences.en: And this is the paradise that Murasaki believes could be hers, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是紫式部相信属于她的天堂，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, and Genji.
sentences.zh: 是的，还有源氏。

sentences.en: And they hope that they will meet and be able to renew their love there.
sentences.zh: 他们希望在那里重逢，并能延续他们的爱情。

sentences.en: So on her deathbed, Murasaki mourns that she would go alone into the unknown and the thought filled her with great sorrow.
sentences.zh: 因此，在临终前，紫式部哀叹自己将独自走向未知，这种想法让她感到无比悲伤。

sentences.en: But she, she has consolation from the thought that in due course, Genji will be able to join her.
sentences.zh: 但她从“源氏终将与她团聚”的念头中得到了慰藉。

sentences.en: And Genji tells her that one day we will share one lotus throne in the life to come.
sentences.zh: 源氏告诉她，终有一天，我们会在来世共坐一朵莲花宝座。

sentences.en: That is the hope that he cleaves to, even while he's shadowed by anxiety, that of course he may not attain it.
sentences.zh: 这就是他所坚守的希望，尽管他内心深处被焦虑笼罩，担心自己或许无法实现这一愿望。

sentences.en: And so this sense of the yearning for things that have gone, a sense that things that go must go,
sentences.zh: 因此，这种对逝去事物的渴望，一种“凡是离去必将离去”的感悟，

sentences.en: a sense that everything is insubstantial, an awareness that time is a kind of treacherous dimension,
sentences.zh: 一种万物皆无常的认知，一种意识到时间是一种诡谲维度的觉知，

sentences.en: all these things that kind of echo, you know, great modern European writers, Proust and so on.
sentences.zh: 所有这些与普鲁斯特等伟大的现代欧洲作家遥相呼应的东西，

sentences.en: I mean, they derive from the, in the context of Murasaki, from the very specific cultural context in which he is born, lives and dies, as you would expect.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在紫式部的语境下，它们源于她出生、生活和死亡的特定文化背景，这是理所当然的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, I can't recommend The Pillar Book too highly.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我极力推荐《枕草子》。

sentences.en: I loved reading it.
sentences.zh: 我非常喜欢读它。

sentences.en: I think it's an extraordinary work of literature.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一部非凡的文学作品。

sentences.en: And I think what's so joyous about it is not just that you can read it in and of itself as a,
sentences.zh: 我认为它最令人愉悦的地方不仅在于你可以把它当作一本极其精彩有趣的读物来阅读，

sentences.en: as a, as a just a brilliantly entertaining book, but you could hardly find a better window into the world.
sentences.zh: 而且你很难找到比它更好的窗口来窥探那个世界。

sentences.en: This sort of incredibly alien and to us very strange world of, of early medieval Japan.
sentences.zh: 那个对我们来说极其陌生、非常奇特的日本中世纪早期世界。

sentences.en: So, I mean, you loved this, didn't you, Tom?
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，你很喜欢这本书，对吧？

sentences.en: You would never, it's like Trafalgar.
sentences.zh: 你永远不会……这就像特拉法尔加海战一样。

sentences.en: It's like something you just, you were sucked into this black hole.
sentences.zh: 就像你被吸进了一个黑洞一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, I did.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: One of the additional reasons why I've so enjoyed doing the series is, as we said earlier,
sentences.zh: 我如此享受制作这个系列节目的另一个原因，正如我们之前所说，

sentences.en: I cannot think of a greater contrast to the six part epic that you are going to be leading directly after this, which is on Peter the Great.
sentences.zh: 我想不出还有什么比你接下来要主持的关于彼得大帝的六集史诗节目对比更强烈的了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: If you enjoy battles, the Great Northern War, the rise of Russia and the decline of the Swedish Empire,
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢战争、大北方战争、俄罗斯的崛起和瑞典帝国的衰落，

sentences.en: dwarfs being baked in pies, people having bellows inserted into them,
sentences.zh: 还有把侏儒烤进馅饼里、往人身体里塞风箱这种事，

sentences.en: Peter the Great going on holiday to the Dutch Republic and to England in disguise.
sentences.zh: 以及彼得大帝乔装打扮去荷兰共和国和英国度假的故事，

sentences.en: If you'd like the sound of all that, you can hear all six parts on Monday by signing up to the Rest is History Club at therestishistory.com.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢听这些，周一就可以通过在 therestishistory.com 注册“历史其余部分俱乐部”来收听全部六集节目。

sentences.en: And if you do that, Tom, you will be welcomed into an imperial court of almost unparalleled beauty and sophistication.
sentences.zh: 如果你那样做了，汤姆，你将受到一个拥有无与伦比的美丽与精致的帝国宫廷的欢迎。

sentences.en: That's right, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是这样吧？

sentences.en: Oh, so beautiful.
sentences.zh: 噢，太美了。

sentences.en: So sophisticated.
sentences.zh: 太精致了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, on that characteristically humble note, I will say arigato, Tom, and sayonara.
sentences.zh: 好吧，带着这种一贯谦逊的调子，我要说声阿里嘎多，汤姆，再见（Sayonara）。

sentences.en: Sayonara.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Sayonara.
sentences.zh: 再见。
